akhfash:3-3.t: He said ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجْوَى﴾: it is as though He said ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ﴾ (and they kept secret) and then explained it afterwards, saying: "they are ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ﴾". Or this comes according to the dialect of those who say "ضَرَبُونِي قَوْمُكَ" (your people struck me, with the plural marker on the verb).

akhfash:30-30.t:
And He said ﴿أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقاً﴾: He said ﴿كَانَتَا﴾ (dual) because He made them two kinds, like the Arabs' saying: "هُما لِقاحانِ سُودَان" (they are two black herds of milch camels), and in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ أَن تَزُولاَ﴾. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 250]:
رَأَوْا جَبَلاً فَوْقَ الجِبالِ إِذا الْتَقَتْ * رُؤُوسُ كَبِيَرِيْهنَّ يَنْتَطِحَانِ
(They saw a mountain above the mountains: when the heads of their two great ones met, they butted each other.)
He said "رُؤوسُ" (heads, plural) and then said "يَنْتَطِحانِ" (dual). This is like the Arabs' saying "الجُزُراتِ" and "الطُرُقاَتِ" (plurals of plurals), so in this you may say "طُرُقانِ" for two (sets) and "جُزُرانِ" for two. The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is poetic witness no. 251]:
وإِذاَ الرِّجَالُ رَأَوْا يَزِيدَ رَأَيْتَهُم * خُضْعَ الرِّقابِ نَواكِسِي الأَبْصارِ
(When men see Yazīd, you see them with humbled necks and downcast eyes.)
And the Arabs say "مَوَاليِات" and "صَواَحِبَاتُ يوسُف" (the female companions of Joseph). These have formed a broken plural and then pluralised "صَواحِب" again; in this way the masculine would be "صَواحِبُون", and its counterpart is "نَواكِسي". Some say "نواكِسِ" in the genitive position, as you say "حُجْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ" (the burrow of a lizard, ruined, with the adjective genitive by proximity).

akhfash:37-37.t: And He said ﴿خُلِقَ ٱلإنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ سَأُوْرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾: He means "from a hastening of the command", because He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا قَوْلُنَا لِشَيْءٍ إِذَآ أَرَدْنَاهُ أَن نَّقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ﴾. So this haste is like His word ﴿فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ﴾, and His word ﴿فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾, for ﴿سَأُوْرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي﴾.

akhfash:63-63.t: And He said ﴿فَاسْأَلُوهُمْ إِن كَانُواْ يِنْطِقُونَ﴾: He used the masculine (rational plural) for the idols though they are inanimate, because in their view they were among those who reason or speak.

akhfash:82-82.t:
And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلشَّيَاطِينِ مَن يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ﴾: He used the masculine (rational plural) for the devils though they are not of humankind, except that they are like them in obedience and disobedience. Do you not see that you say "الشياطينُ يَعْصُونَ" (the devils disobey) and do not say "يَعْصِينَ" (feminine plural)? He made ﴿يَغُوصُونَ﴾ plural while ﴿مَنْ﴾ is singular in form, because ﴿مَنْ﴾ in meaning refers to a group. The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is poetic witness no. 248]:
لَسْنَا كَمَنْ جَعَلَتْ إِيادٍ دارَهَا * تكريت تَنْظُرُ حَبَّها أَنْ يُحَصَدا
(We are not like those of Iyād who made Takrīt their home, waiting for their grain to be harvested.)
And he said [in the mutaqārib metre; this is poetic witness no. 249]:
أَطُوفُ بِهَا لاَ أَرَىَ غَيْرَهَا * كَمَا طافَ بالبِيْعَةِ الرّاهِبِ
(I circle around her, seeing no one else, as the monk circles round the church.)
He made "الراهبِ" a badal (substitute) for ﴿مَا﴾, as though he said "like the one who circled". «[Translator's note: ﴿مَا﴾ here refers to the «ما» of «كما» in the verse.]» And the Arabs say: "إِنَّ الحَقَّ مَنْ صَدَّقَ اللهَ" (the right is he who believes Allah), i.e. "the right is the right of him who believes Allah".

akhfash:87-87.t: And He said ﴿إِذ ذَّهَبَ مُغَاضِباً فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ﴾, i.e. that We would not decree punishment for him, because he had sinned by leaving his people. He was angry only with some of the kings; he was not angry with his Lord — he knew Allah, Mighty and Majestic, better than that.

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿وَ﴾ and mention Maryam, ﴿الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا﴾ she guarded it from being touched, ﴿فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ رُوحِنَا﴾ i.e. Jibrīl, when he blew into the opening of the neck of her shift, so she conceived ʿĪsā, ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا وَابْنَهَا آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ humans, jinn and angels, since she bore him without a male.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذِهِ﴾ i.e. the religion of Islam ﴿أُمَّتُكُمْ﴾ is your religion, O you who are addressed, i.e. you must hold to it, ﴿أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ a permanent ḥāl (circumstantial), ﴿وَأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾ affirm My oneness.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿وَتَقَطَّعُوا﴾ i.e. some of those addressed ﴿أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ i.e. they split up the affair of their religion, differing over it; they are the sects of the Jews and the Christians. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿كُلٌّ إِلَيْنَا رَاجِعُونَ﴾ i.e. and We shall recompense each for his deeds.

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا كُفْرَانَ﴾ i.e. no denial ﴿لِسَعْيِهِ وَإِنَّا لَهُ كَاتِبُونَ﴾ in that We command the recording angels to write it down, and We shall recompense him for it.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿وَحَرَامٌ عَلَى قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا﴾ its people are meant ﴿أَنَّهُمْ لَا﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ i.e. their return to this world is impossible.

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿حَتَّى﴾ marks the limit of the impossibility of their return ﴿إِذَا فُتِحَتْ﴾ read without and with doubling [of the tāʾ] ﴿يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ﴾ with the hamza and without it; two foreign names of two tribes, and a muḍāf is implied before it, i.e. their barrier; and that is near the Resurrection, ﴿وَهُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ حَدَبٍ﴾ raised ground ﴿يَنْسِلُونَ﴾ they hasten.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿وَاقْتَرَبَ الْوَعْدُ الْحَقُّ﴾ i.e. the Day of Resurrection, ﴿فَإِذَا هِيَ﴾ i.e. the matter [al-qiṣṣa] ﴿شَاخِصَةٌ أَبْصَارُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ on that Day because of its severity; they say: ﴿يَا﴾ for calling attention ﴿وَيْلَنَا﴾ our ruin! ﴿قَدْ كُنَّا﴾ in the world ﴿فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هَذَا﴾ Day; ﴿بَلْ كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ to ourselves, by our denying the messengers.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him, of the idols, ﴿حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ are its fuel; ﴿أَنْتُمْ لَهَا وَارِدُونَ﴾ entering it.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ idols ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ as you claim, ﴿مَا وَرَدُوهَا﴾ they would not have entered it; ﴿وَكُلٌّ﴾ of the worshippers and the worshipped ﴿فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ for the worshippers ﴿فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا لَا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ anything, because of the intensity of its boiling. And [the following] was revealed when Ibn al-Zibaʿrā said: ʿUzayr, the Messiah and the angels have been worshipped, so they are in the Fire according to what preceded.

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا﴾ the rank ﴿الْحُسْنَى﴾ and among them are those mentioned, ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿لَا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَهَا﴾ its sound, ﴿وَهُمْ فِي مَا اشْتَهَتْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ of bliss ﴿خَالِدُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿لَا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الْفَزَعُ الْأَكْبَرُ﴾ which is when the servant is ordered off to the Fire, ﴿وَتَتَلَقَّاهُمْ﴾ receives them ﴿الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ when they come out of the graves, saying to them: ﴿هَذَا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ in the world.

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ accusative (manṣūb) by «اذكر» (mention) implied (muqaddar) before it ﴿نَطْوِي السَّمَاءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ﴾ the name of an angel ﴿لِلْكِتَابِ﴾ the scroll of the son of Adam at his death, and the lām is redundant (zāʾida); or al-sijill is the scroll and al-kitāb is in the sense of «مكتوب» (what is written), and the lām is in the sense of «على». In one reading [لِلْكُتُبِ] as a plural. ﴿كَمَا بَدَأْنَا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ﴾ from nothing ﴿نُعِيدُهُ﴾ after annihilating it; so the kāf is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نعيد», its pronoun refers back to «أول», and «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). ﴿وَعْدًا عَلَيْنَا﴾ accusative by «وعدنا» implied before it, and it emphasises the content of what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ﴾ what We have promised.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِي الزَّبُورِ﴾ in the sense of «الكتاب», i.e. the revealed books of Allah, ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ﴾ in the sense of the Mother of the Book which is with Allah, ﴿أَنَّ الْأَرْضَ﴾ the land of the Garden ﴿يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِيَ الصَّالِحُونَ﴾ general, covering every righteous person.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي هَذَا﴾ Qurʾān ﴿لَبَلَاغًا﴾ sufficiency for entering the Garden ﴿لِقَوْمٍ عَابِدِينَ﴾ who act by it.

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿إِلَّا رَحْمَةً﴾ i.e. for mercy ﴿لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ humans and jinn, through you.

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ﴾ i.e. nothing is revealed to me concerning the God except His oneness. ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ submitting to what is revealed to me of the oneness of the God? The question is in the sense of a command.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from that, ﴿فَقُلْ آذَنْتُكُمْ﴾ of war ﴿عَلَى سَوَاءٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from both the fāʿil (agent) and the mafʿūl (object), i.e. equal in knowledge of it; I do not keep it to myself apart from you, so that you may make ready. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ أَمْ بَعِيدٌ مَا تُوعَدُونَ﴾ of punishment, or the Resurrection which includes it; only Allah knows it.

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ the Exalted ﴿يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ and deed, from you and from others, ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْتُمُونَ﴾ you and others, of what is secret.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَدْرِي لَعَلَّهُ﴾ i.e. what I have informed you of, whose time is not known, ﴿فِتْنَةٌ﴾ a test ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ so that He may see how you act, ﴿وَمَتَاعٌ﴾ enjoyment ﴿إِلَى حِينٍ﴾ i.e. the ending of your lifespans. This is set against the first, which is hoped for with «لعل»; the second is not a place for hoping.

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ and in one reading [قَالَ] ﴿رَبِّ احْكُمْ﴾ between me and those who deny me ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ with punishment for them or victory over them; so they were punished at Badr, Uḥud, al-Aḥzāb, Ḥunayn and al-Khandaq, and he was given victory over them. ﴿وَرَبُّنَا الرَّحْمَنُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَى مَا تَصِفُونَ﴾ of your lying against Allah in your saying "He has taken a son", and against me in your saying "a sorcerer", and against the Qurʾān in your saying "poetry". [Translator's note: al-Aḥzāb and al-Khandaq are usually names of the same battle; the source lists them separately.]

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿اقْتَرَبَ﴾ — has drawn near — ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ — the people of Mecca, deniers of the resurrection — ﴿حِسَابُهُمْ﴾ — on the Day of Resurrection — ﴿وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ﴾ — about it — ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ — from preparing for it through faith.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ مُحْدَثٍ﴾ — little by little, i.e. the wording of the Quran — ﴿إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ — mocking,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿لَاهِيَةً﴾ — heedless — ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ — of its meaning. ﴿وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى﴾ — i.e. the talk — ﴿الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ — a badal (substitute) from the wāw of "wa-asarrū al-najwā": ﴿هَلْ هَذَا﴾ — i.e. Muḥammad — ﴿إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ﴾ — so what he brings is sorcery? ﴿أَفَتَأْتُونَ السِّحْرَ﴾ — follow it — ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ — knowing that it is sorcery?

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — to them — ﴿رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ الْقَوْلَ﴾ — being — ﴿فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ — of what they kept secret — ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ — of it.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ — for transition from one purpose to another, in the three places — ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — about the Quran he brought: it is — ﴿أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ﴾ — jumbles he saw in sleep — ﴿بَلِ افْتَرَاهُ﴾ — fabricated it — ﴿بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ﴾ — so what he brought is poetry. ﴿فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِآيَةٍ كَمَا أُرْسِلَ الْأَوَّلُونَ﴾ — such as the she-camel, the staff and the hand. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿مَا آمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ — i.e. its people — ﴿أَهْلَكْنَاهَا﴾ — for denying the signs that came to it. ﴿أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — No.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا يُوحَى﴾ — and in one reading [نُوحِي], with nūn and kasra on the ḥāʾ — ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ — not angels. ﴿فَاسْأَلُوا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ﴾ — those learned in the Torah and the Gospel — ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — that, for they know it, and you are closer to believing them than to believing the believers in Muḥammad.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ﴾ — the messengers — ﴿جَسَدًا﴾ — meaning bodies — ﴿لَا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ﴾ — rather they eat it — ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا خَالِدِينَ﴾ — in the world.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَاهُمُ الْوَعْدَ﴾ — of saving them — ﴿فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُمْ وَمَنْ نَشَاءُ﴾ — i.e. those who believed them — ﴿وَأَهْلَكْنَا الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ — those who denied them.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ — O company of Quraysh — ﴿كِتَابًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ﴾ — because it is in your language. ﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ — and so believe in it?

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا﴾ — We destroyed — ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ — i.e. its people — ﴿كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً﴾ — disbelieving — ﴿وَأَنْشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا آخَرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوا بَأْسَنَا﴾ — i.e. the people of the town sensed the destruction — ﴿إِذَا هُمْ مِنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ﴾ — fleeing in haste. So the angels said to them mockingly:

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿لَا تَرْكُضُوا وَارْجِعُوا إِلَى مَا أُتْرِفْتُمْ﴾ — you were given luxury — ﴿فِيهِ وَمَسَاكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْأَلُونَ﴾ — for something of your worldly goods, as usual.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا﴾ — for calling attention (li-l-tanbīh) — ﴿وَيْلَنَا﴾ — our destruction! ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ — through disbelief.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿فَمَا زَالَتْ تِلْكَ﴾ — words — ﴿دَعْوَاهُمْ﴾ — they called out with them and repeated them — ﴿حَتَّى جَعَلْنَاهُمْ حَصِيدًا﴾ — i.e. like crops reaped with sickles, by their being killed with the sword — ﴿خَامِدِينَ﴾ — dead, like the dying down of fire when it is extinguished.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ﴾ — in idle play, but rather as pointing to Our power and benefiting Our servants.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿لَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا﴾ — something to divert oneself with, such as a wife or a child — ﴿لَاتَّخَذْنَاهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾ — from Our presence, from the wide-eyed houris and the angels — ﴿إِنْ كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ﴾ — that; but We did not do it, so We did not will it.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿بَلْ نَقْذِفُ﴾ — We hurl — ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — faith — ﴿عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ﴾ — disbelief — ﴿فَيَدْمَغُهُ﴾ — removes it — ﴿فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ﴾ — vanishing. Damaghahu originally means "struck his brain (dimāgh)", which is a fatal spot. ﴿وَلَكُمْ﴾ — O disbelievers of Mecca — ﴿الْوَيْلُ﴾ — severe punishment — ﴿مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ﴾ — Allah with, of a wife or a child.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ — the Exalted — ﴿مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ — as possession. ﴿وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ﴾ — i.e. the angels; a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ﴾ — they do not grow weary.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ﴾ — from it; for it is to them like breathing is to us: nothing distracts us from it.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ — meaning "bal" (rather), for transition, and the hamza for disapproval (inkār) — ﴿اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً﴾ — being — ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ — such as stone, gold and silver — ﴿هُمْ﴾ — i.e. the gods — ﴿يُنْشِرُونَ﴾ — i.e. bring the dead to life? No; and none is a god except one who brings the dead to life.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا﴾ — i.e. the heavens and the earth — ﴿آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ — i.e. other than Him — ﴿لَفَسَدَتَا﴾ — they would have departed from their observed order, because of the mutual obstruction among them, in accordance with what usually happens when there are several rulers: mutual obstruction in a matter and lack of agreement on it. ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ﴾ — exalted above all is — ﴿اللَّهِ رَبِّ﴾ — the Creator of — ﴿الْعَرْشِ﴾ — the Throne (al-kursī) — ﴿عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ﴾ — the disbelievers, Allah with, of a partner to Him and other things.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ﴾ — about their deeds.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ — the Exalted, i.e. besides Him — ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ — in it is an interrogative of rebuke (istifhām tawbīkh). ﴿قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ﴾ — for that; and there is no way to it. ﴿هَذَا ذِكْرُ مَنْ مَعِيَ﴾ — i.e. my community, and it is the Quran — ﴿وَذِكْرُ مَنْ قَبْلِي﴾ — of the nations, and it is the Torah, the Gospel and others of the books of Allah; in none of them is it [stated] that there is a god with Allah of the kind they claimed — He is exalted above that. ﴿بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْحَقَّ﴾ — i.e. the oneness of Allah — ﴿فَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ — from the reflection that leads to it.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا يُوحَى﴾ — and in one reading [نُوحِي], with nūn and kasra on the ḥāʾ — ﴿إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾ — i.e. affirm My oneness.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدًا﴾ — from among the angels. ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ﴾ — they are — ﴿عِبَادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ﴾ — with Him; and servitude is incompatible with being begotten.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ — they do not utter their speech except after His speech — ﴿وَهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ — i.e. after it.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ — i.e. what they have done and what they will do — ﴿وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ارْتَضَى﴾ — the Exalted, that intercession be made for him — ﴿وَهُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ﴾ — the Exalted — ﴿مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ — fearful.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّي إِلَهٌ مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ — i.e. Allah, i.e. other than Him; and he is Iblīs, who called to the worship of himself and commanded obedience to himself — ﴿فَذَلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ كَذَلِكَ﴾ — just as We requite him — ﴿نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ — i.e. the idolaters.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾ — with wāw and without it — ﴿يَرَ﴾ — know — ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا﴾ — i.e. a closed mass, meaning closed up — ﴿فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا﴾ — We made the heaven seven and the earth seven; or the opening of the heaven, in that it used not to rain and then it rained, and the opening of the earth, in that it used not to grow plants and then it grew them. ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ﴾ — which descends from the sky and springs from the earth — ﴿كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ — of plants and other things; i.e. water is a cause of its life. ﴿أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — in My oneness?

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ﴾ — firm mountains — so that ﴿أَنْ﴾ — not — ﴿تَمِيدَ﴾ — move — ﴿بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا﴾ — i.e. the mountains — ﴿فِجَاجًا﴾ — passages — ﴿سُبُلًا﴾ — a badal (substitute), i.e. wide through-roads — ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ — to their destinations on journeys.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا﴾ — for the earth, like the roof of a house — ﴿مَحْفُوظًا﴾ — from falling. ﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا﴾ — the sun, the moon and the stars — ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ — they do not reflect on them so as to know that their Creator has no partner.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ﴾ — its tanwīn is a replacement for the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct): of the sun and the moon and what follows them, namely the stars — ﴿فِي فَلَكٍ﴾ — i.e. a circular one, like a millstone, in the sky — ﴿يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ — move swiftly, like one swimming in water; and because of the comparison with him, He used the pronoun of the plural of rational beings. And the following was revealed when the disbelievers said, "Muḥammad will die":

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ﴾ — i.e. remaining forever in the world. ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ﴾ — in it? No. So the last clause is the locus of the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī).

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ﴾ — in the world. ﴿وَنَبْلُوكُمْ﴾ — We test you — ﴿بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ﴾ — such as poverty and wealth, sickness and health — ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾ — a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. so that We may see whether you will be patient and grateful or not. ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ — and We will requite you.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ﴾ — "not" — ﴿يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا﴾ — i.e. an object of mockery, saying: ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ — i.e. finds fault with them? ﴿وَهُمْ بِذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ — to them — ﴿هُمْ﴾ — a tawkīd (emphasis) — ﴿كَافِرُونَ﴾ — of it, since they said, "We do not know him." And the following was revealed about their seeking to hasten the punishment:

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾ — i.e. because of his great haste in his affairs, it is as if he were created from it. ﴿سَأُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي﴾ — My promises of punishment — ﴿فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾ — about it. So He showed them killing at Badr.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ — of the Resurrection — ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ — in it? The Exalted said:

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ﴾ — ward off — ﴿عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ — protected from it at the Resurrection; and the jawāb (apodosis) of "law" is: they would not have said that.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ﴾ — the Resurrection — ﴿بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ﴾ — bewilders them — ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ — given respite for repentance or excuse.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ — in it is consolation for the Prophet ﷺ — ﴿فَحَاقَ﴾ — descended — ﴿بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ — and it is the punishment; so likewise it will descend upon whoever mocks you.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ — to them — ﴿مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ﴾ — protects you — ﴿بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ — from His punishment, if it descends upon you? I.e. no one does that. And those addressed do not fear Allah's punishment because they deny it. ﴿بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — i.e. the Quran — ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ — they do not reflect on it.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ — in it is the meaning of the hamza, for disapproval, i.e. "a-" — ﴿لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ﴾ — from what would harm them — ﴿مِنْ دُونِنَا﴾ — i.e. do they have anyone other than Us who protects them from it? ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ — i.e. the gods — ﴿نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ — so they will not help them — ﴿وَلَا هُمْ﴾ — i.e. the disbelievers — ﴿مِنَّا﴾ — from Our punishment — ﴿يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ — given protection; one says "ṣaḥibaka Allāh", i.e. may He guard you and protect you.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ وَآبَاءَهُمْ﴾ — with what We bestowed on them — ﴿حَتَّى طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ﴾ — and they were deluded by that. ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ﴾ — We aim at their land — ﴿نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ — by conquest for the Prophet? ﴿أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ — No; rather the Prophet and his Companions.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ — to them — ﴿إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ﴾ — from Allah, not from myself. ﴿وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ إِذَا﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second lightened (tashīl) between it and yāʾ — ﴿مَا يُنْذَرُونَ﴾ — i.e. they, because they abandon acting upon the warning they have heard, are like the deaf.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ﴾ — a light blow — ﴿مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَا﴾ — for calling attention (li-l-tanbīh) — ﴿وَيْلَنَا﴾ — our destruction! ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ — through associating partners and denying Muḥammad.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ﴾ — possessing justice — ﴿لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ — i.e. on it — ﴿فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا﴾ — by the reduction of a good deed or the addition of a bad deed. ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ﴾ — the deed — ﴿مِثْقَالَ﴾ — the weight of — ﴿حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا﴾ — with what is to be weighed of it. ﴿وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ﴾ — reckoning everything precisely.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ﴾ — i.e. the Torah, which distinguishes between truth and falsehood, the lawful and the unlawful — ﴿وَضِيَاءً﴾ — through it — ﴿وَذِكْرًا﴾ — i.e. an admonition through it — ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ — out of sight of people, i.e. in private away from them — ﴿وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ﴾ — i.e. its terrors — ﴿مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ — i.e. fearful.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَهَذَا﴾ — i.e. the Quran — ﴿ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ﴾ — the interrogative in it is for rebuke (tawbīkh).

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ رُشْدَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ — i.e. his guidance, before he reached maturity — ﴿وَكُنَّا بِهِ عَالِمِينَ﴾ — i.e. that he was worthy of that.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا هَذِهِ التَّمَاثِيلُ﴾ — the idols — ﴿الَّتِي أَنْتُمْ لَهَا عَاكِفُونَ﴾ — i.e. persisting in worshipping them?

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿قَالُوا وَجَدْنَا آبَاءَنَا لَهَا عَابِدِينَ﴾ — so we followed their example.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — to them — ﴿لَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ﴾ — by worshipping them — ﴿فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ — clear.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿قَالُوا أَجِئْتَنَا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — in this saying of yours — ﴿أَمْ أَنْتَ مِنَ اللَّاعِبِينَ﴾ — in it?

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿قَالَ بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ — who is deserving of worship — ﴿رَبُّ﴾ — is the Owner of — ﴿السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ﴾ — created them without any previous model — ﴿وَأَنَا عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ﴾ — which I have said — ﴿مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾ — to it.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَتَاللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَامَكُمْ بَعْدَ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا مُدْبِرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُمْ﴾ — after they had gone to their gathering on a feast day of theirs — ﴿جُذَاذًا﴾ — with ḍamma on the jīm and with kasra on it; fragments, with an axe — ﴿إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَهُمْ﴾ — he hung the axe on its neck — ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ — i.e. to the big one — ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ — and see what it did to the others.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — after their return and their seeing what had been done — ﴿مَنْ فَعَلَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ — in it.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — i.e. some of them to others — ﴿سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ﴾ — i.e. finding fault with them — ﴿يُقَالُ لَهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿قَالُوا فَأْتُوا بِهِ عَلَى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ﴾ — i.e. openly — ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ — against him, that he is the one who did it.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — to him, after he was brought — ﴿أَأَنْتَ﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, with the second changed into an alif, and with it lightened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between the lightened one and the other, and without it — ﴿فَعَلْتَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — keeping silent about his own deed — ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَذَا فَاسْأَلُوهُمْ﴾ — about who did it — ﴿إِنْ كَانُوا يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ — in it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) placed first; and in what precedes it is an allusion to them that an idol known to be incapable of acting cannot be a god.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿فَرَجَعُوا إِلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ — through reflection — ﴿فَقَالُوا﴾ — to themselves — ﴿إِنَّكُمْ أَنْتُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ — i.e. by your worshipping what does not speak.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا﴾ — by Allah — ﴿عَلَى رُءُوسِهِمْ﴾ — i.e. they were returned to their disbelief, and they said: by Allah, ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ — i.e. so how can you order us to ask them?

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ — i.e. instead of Him — ﴿مَا لَا يَنْفَعُكُمْ شَيْئًا﴾ — of provision and other things — ﴿وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ﴾ — in anything, if you do not worship it?

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿أُفٍّ﴾ — with kasra on the fāʾ and with fatḥa on it; in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. stench and ugliness — ﴿لَكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ — i.e. other than Him. ﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ — that these idols do not deserve worship and are not fit for it, and that only Allah the Exalted deserves it?

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿قَالُوا حَرِّقُوهُ﴾ — i.e. Ibrāhīm — ﴿وَانْصُرُوا آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ — i.e. by burning him — ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ﴾ — helping them. So they gathered a great deal of firewood for him and set all of it ablaze, and they bound Ibrāhīm, put him in a catapult and threw him into the fire. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿قُلْنَا يَا نَارُ كُونِي بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ — so it burned nothing of him except his bonds; its heat went away and its light remained. And by His saying {وَسَلَامًا} he was kept safe from dying of its coldness.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿وَأَرَادُوا بِهِ كَيْدًا﴾ — and that was the burning — ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُمُ الْأَخْسَرِينَ﴾ — in what they intended.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَلُوطًا﴾ — the son of his brother Hārān — from Iraq ﴿إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ — with abundant rivers and trees; and it is Syria (al-Shām). Ibrāhīm settled in Palestine and Lūṭ in al-Muʾtafika, and between them is a day's [journey].

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ﴾ — i.e. to Ibrāhīm; and he had asked for a child, as mentioned in al-Ṣāffāt — ﴿إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً﴾ — i.e. in addition to what was asked for; or it is the child's child — ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾ — i.e. him and his two sons — ﴿جَعَلْنَا صَالِحِينَ﴾ — prophets.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَئِمَّةً﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second changed into a yāʾ; who are followed in good — ﴿يَهْدُونَ﴾ — people — ﴿بِأَمْرِنَا﴾ — to Our religion — ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ الْخَيْرَاتِ وَإِقَامَ الصَّلَوةِ وَإِيتَاءَ الزَّكَوةِ﴾ — i.e. that they be done, established and given, by them and by their followers; and the dropping of the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) of "iqāma" is for lightness — ﴿وَكَانُوا لَنَا عَابِدِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَلُوطًا آتَيْنَاهُ حُكْمًا﴾ — judgement between disputants — ﴿وَعِلْمًا وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ تَعْمَلُ﴾ — i.e. its people, the deeds — ﴿الْخَبَائِثَ﴾ — of sodomy, shooting with pellets, playing with birds and other than that. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ﴾ — the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "sāʾahu" (it grieved him), the opposite of "sarrahu" (it pleased him) — ﴿فَاسِقِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَأَدْخَلْنَاهُ فِي رَحْمَتِنَا﴾ — in that We saved him from his people. ﴿إِنَّهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿نُوحًا﴾ — and what follows is a badal (substitute) from it — ﴿إِذْ نَادَى﴾ — invoked against his people with his saying {رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْ}, etc. — ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ — i.e. before Ibrāhīm and Lūṭ — ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ﴾ — who were in his ark — ﴿مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ — i.e. drowning, and his people's denial of him.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿وَنَصَرْنَاهُ﴾ — We protected him — ﴿مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ — which prove his messengership — so that they could not reach him with harm. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿دَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ﴾ — i.e. their story; and there is substituted (badal) from them — ﴿إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِي الْحَرْثِ﴾ — it was crops or a vineyard — ﴿إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ الْقَوْمِ﴾ — i.e. grazed in it at night without a shepherd, having got loose — ﴿وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَاهِدِينَ﴾ — in it is the use of the plural pronoun for two. Dāwūd said: the owner of the field gets the sheep themselves. Sulaymān said: he benefits from their milk, offspring and wool until the field returns to what it was, through its [the sheep's] owner restoring it, and then he returns them to him.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا﴾ — i.e. the judgement — ﴿سُلَيْمَانَ﴾ — and the judgement of both was by ijtihād (independent reasoning), and Dāwūd deferred to Sulaymān; and it is said it was by revelation, the second abrogating the first. ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾ — of the two — ﴿آتَيْنَا﴾ — him — ﴿حُكْمًا﴾ — prophethood — ﴿وَعِلْمًا﴾ — of the matters of religion. ﴿وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُدَ الْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَالطَّيْرَ﴾ — likewise; both were made subject to glorify with him, at his command, whenever he felt slackness, so that he would be invigorated for it. ﴿وَكُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ﴾ — the subjecting of them to glorify with him, even if it is a wonder to you, i.e. their answering the master Dāwūd.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ﴾ — and it is the coat of mail, because it is worn (tulbas); he was the first to make it, and before it there were plates — ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ — among all people — ﴿لِنُحْصِنَكُمْ﴾ — with nūn, referring to Allah; with the lower-dotted letter (yāʾ), referring to Dāwūd; and with the upper-dotted letter (tāʾ) [لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ], referring to the mail — ﴿مِنْ بَأْسِكُمْ﴾ — your war with your enemies. ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ﴾ — O people of Mecca — ﴿شَاكِرُونَ﴾ — My blessings, by believing the Messenger? I.e. thank Me by that.

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — We subjected — ﴿لِسُلَيْمَانَ الرِّيحَ عَاصِفَةً﴾ — and in another verse "rukhāʾan" (gently), i.e. blowing strongly or lightly according to his will — ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا﴾ — and it is Syria (al-Shām). ﴿وَكُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَالِمِينَ﴾ — among that is His knowledge, the Exalted, that what He gives Sulaymān calls him to humility before his Lord; so His action, the Exalted, is in accordance with what His knowledge requires.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — We subjected — ﴿مِنَ الشَّيَاطِينِ مَنْ يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ﴾ — they enter the sea and bring out jewels from it for Sulaymān — ﴿وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًا دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ — i.e. other than diving, such as building and other things — ﴿وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَافِظِينَ﴾ — from spoiling what they had made, because whenever they finished a task before nightfall they would spoil it if they were not occupied with something else.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿أَيُّوبَ﴾ — and there is substituted (badal) from it — ﴿إِذْ نَادَى رَبَّهُ﴾ — when he was afflicted with the loss of all his wealth and children, the tearing of his body, and all people deserting him except his wife, for three years, or seven, or eighteen, and with the hardship of his living — ﴿أَنِّي﴾ — with fatḥa on the hamza, with the implied bāʾ — ﴿مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ﴾ — i.e. hardship — ﴿وَأَنْتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ﴾ — his call — ﴿فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِ مِنْ ضُرٍّ وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَهْلَهُ﴾ — his children, male and female, in that they were brought back to life for him, each of the two kinds being three or seven — ﴿وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ﴾ — from his wife, whose youth was increased. He had a threshing floor for wheat and a threshing floor for barley, so Allah sent two clouds: one of them poured gold onto the wheat floor and the other poured silver onto the barley floor until it overflowed — ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ — a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) — ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنَا﴾ — an adjective (ṣifa) — ﴿وَذِكْرَى لِلْعَابِدِينَ﴾ — so that they may be patient and be rewarded.

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ — in obedience to Allah and in refraining from disobeying Him.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَأَدْخَلْنَاهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِنَا﴾ — of prophethood. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ — for it. He was named Dhū al-Kifl because he took upon himself (takaffala) to fast all his days, to stand in prayer all his nights, and to judge between people without becoming angry; and he fulfilled that. And it is said that he was not a prophet.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿ذَا النُّونِ﴾ — the one of the fish, and he is Yūnus ibn Mattā; and there is substituted (badal) from it — ﴿إِذْ ذَهَبَ مُغَاضِبًا﴾ — with his people, i.e. angry with them for what he had endured from them, and he had not been given permission for that — ﴿فَظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ نَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ — i.e. that We would not decree against him what We decreed, of confining him in the belly of the fish, or constrain him with that. ﴿فَنَادَى فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ — the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea and the darkness of the fish's belly — ﴿أَنْ﴾ — i.e. "bi-an" (saying that) — ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ — in my leaving from among my people without permission.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ﴾ — by those words. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — just as We saved him — ﴿نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — from their distress, when they call on Us for help in supplication.

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿زَكَرِيَّا﴾ — and there is substituted (badal) from it — ﴿إِذْ نَادَى رَبَّهُ﴾ — by saying — ﴿رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِي فَرْدًا﴾ — i.e. without a child to inherit from me — ﴿وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْوَارِثِينَ﴾ — the One who remains after Your creation has perished.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ﴾ — his call — ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ يَحْيَى﴾ — as a son — ﴿وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ﴾ — so she bore the child after her barrenness. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ — i.e. the prophets mentioned — ﴿كَانُوا يُسَارِعُونَ﴾ — hastening — ﴿فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ﴾ — acts of obedience — ﴿وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا﴾ — in Our mercy — ﴿وَرَهَبًا﴾ — of Our punishment — ﴿وَكَانُوا لَنَا خَاشِعِينَ﴾ — humble in their worship.

daas-irab:1-3.t: ﴿اقْتَرَبَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) اقترب. ﴿حِسابُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and هم is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي غَفْلَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to معرضون. ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿يَأْتِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿ذِكْرٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, as fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to a naʿt (adjective) of ذكر. ﴿مُحْدَثٍ﴾ a second naʿt. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿اسْتَمَعُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial and هم is mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of هم, and the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿لاهِيَةً﴾ a ḥāl from the wāw in يلعبون. ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil of لاهية. ﴿وَأَسَرُّوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and أسروا is a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿النَّجْوَى﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, badal (substitute) from the fāʿil of أسروا; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative noun. [Translator's note: the source calls هل a noun (اسم); it is ordinarily classed as an interrogative particle.] ﴿هذا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿بَشَرٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿مِثْلُكُمْ﴾ a naʿt, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَفَتَأْتُونَ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation and the fāʾ is a conjunction; an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿السِّحْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ, and the wāw is circumstantial. ﴿تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:4-5.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبِّي﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْقَوْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِي السَّماءِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from القول. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and [it is] maʿṭūf (conjoined) to السماء. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; هو is mubtadaʾ. ﴿السَّمِيعُ﴾ khabar. ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ a second khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَضْغاثُ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿أَحْلامٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression. ﴿افْتَراهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿شاعِرٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿فَلْيَأْتِنا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), the lām is for command, and يأتنا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by deletion of the weak letter; نا is its object and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِآيَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to يأتنا; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿كَما﴾ ما is relative; [the kāf and ما] are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of آية. ﴿أُرْسِلَ الْأَوَّلُونَ﴾ a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-9.t: ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿آمَنَتْ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; the clause is resumptive. ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿قَرْيَةٍ﴾ a noun genitive in form, nominative in position, as fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَهْلَكْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a naʿt (adjective). ﴿أَفَهُمْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation and the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿هم﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negating. ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿قَبْلَكَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿رِجالًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿نُوحِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نوحي; the clause نوحي إليهم is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of رجالا. ﴿فَسْئَلُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and اسألوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَهْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الذِّكْرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negating. ﴿جَعَلْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿جَسَداً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَأْكُلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الطَّعامَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of جسد. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negating. ﴿كانُوا﴾ an incomplete past verb, and the wāw is its noun. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ its khabar, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to يأكلون. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿صَدَقْناهُمُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object. ﴿الْوَعْدَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَأَنْجَيْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and [من is] a relative noun conjoined to هم. ﴿نَشاءُ﴾ the clause نشاء is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَأَهْلَكْنَا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:10-12.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām is the response to an omitted oath. ﴿قد﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿أَنْزَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزلنا. ﴿كِتاباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿ذِكْرُكُمْ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of كتابا. ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is for disapproving interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لا is negating. ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿وَكَمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive. ﴿كَمْ﴾ declarative (khabariyya), in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of قصمنا. ﴿قَصَمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ a genitive noun, the tamyīz (specification) of كم. ﴿كانَتْ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿ظالِمَةً﴾ khabar of كان; the clause is a naʿt of قرية. ﴿وَأَنْشَأْنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بَعْدَها﴾ an adverb attached to أنشأنا. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿آخَرِينَ﴾ a naʿt. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لما is the temporal (ḥīniyya) one, an adverb of time. ﴿أَحَسُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بَأْسَنا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِذا﴾ the [إذا] of surprise (fujāʾiyya). ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْها﴾ the two are attached to يركضون. ﴿يَرْكُضُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of هم.

daas-irab:13-16.t: ﴿لا﴾ prohibitive. ﴿تَرْكُضُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech) of an omitted verb. ﴿وَارْجِعُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿ارْجِعُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿إِلى ما﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ارجعوا. ﴿أُتْرِفْتُمْ﴾ a passive past verb and nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to أترفتم. ﴿وَمَساكِنِكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and مساكنكم is a conjoined noun, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ a particle resembling the verb, and the kāf is its noun. ﴿تُسْئَلُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of لعل. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا وَيْلَنا﴾ يا is a vocative particle. ﴿وَيْلَنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), in a genitive construct (muḍāf); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ a particle resembling the verb, and نا is its noun. ﴿كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ﴾ كان, its noun and its khabar; the clause is the khabar of إن. ﴿فَما زالَتْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as its noun. ﴿دَعْواهُمْ﴾ its khabar, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi and the mīm is for the plural; the clause is conjoined. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) taking the genitive. ﴿جَعَلْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿حَصِيداً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿خامِدِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of حصيدا. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negating. ﴿خَلَقْنَا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿السَّماءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to السماء. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is a relative noun conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿لاعِبِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.

daas-irab:17-20.t: ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, not jussive-governing. ﴿أَرَدْنا﴾ a past verb and fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَنْ﴾ accusative-governing. ﴿نَتَّخِذَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being نحن. ﴿لَهْواً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of أردنا. ﴿لَاتَّخَذْناهُ﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو. ﴿اتخذناه﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْ﴾ negating, in the sense of ما. [Translator's note: the Quranic text reads ﴿إِنْ﴾ (in) here; the source writes أن.] ﴿كُنَّا﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿فاعِلِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿نَقْذِفُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to نقذف. ﴿عَلَى الْباطِلِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَيَدْمَغُهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿يدمغه﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿إذا﴾ the [إذا] of surprise (fujāʾiyya). ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿زاهِقٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿وَلَكُمُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿الْوَيْلُ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ﴾ من is a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ relative; the two are attached to the omitted khabar of ويل. ﴿تَصِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun conjoined to من في السموات. ﴿عِنْدَهُ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿عَنْ عِبادَتِهِ﴾ the two are attached to يستكبرون, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negating. ﴿يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّيْلَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to يسبحون. ﴿وَالنَّهارَ﴾ conjoined. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَفْتُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:21-23.t: ﴿أَمِ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اتَّخَذُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of آلهة. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُنْشِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause هم ينشرون is a second naʿt of آلهة. ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, not jussive-governing. ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿فِيهِما﴾ the two are attached to a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿آلِهَةٌ﴾ its postponed noun. ﴿إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ in the sense of غير (other than), in the position of the nominative as a naʿt, with the Name of Majesty as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَفَسَدَتا﴾ the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; a past verb, the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine and the alif is the fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿فَسُبْحانَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿سبحان﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ badal (substitute) from الله. ﴿الْعَرْشِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ عن and the relative ما; the two are attached to سبحان. ﴿يَصِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُسْئَلُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَمَّا﴾ the two are attached to يسأل. ﴿يَفْعَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُسْئَلُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause يسألون is the khabar, and the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is conjoined or a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:24-27.t: ﴿أَمِ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اتَّخَذُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of اتخذوا. ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿هاتُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw of the group is the fāʿil. ﴿بُرْهانَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and the mīm is for the plural. ﴿هذا﴾ the hā is for calling attention (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ذِكْرُ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ﴾ a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. And ﴿مَعِيَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَذِكْرُ﴾ conjoined to the first ذكر. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَبْلِي﴾ an adverb of time attached to the ṣila of the relative noun, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of causation (taʿlīl), and هم is mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ khabar. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive and ما is negating. ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾ من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿رَسُولٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿نُوحِي﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to نوحي. ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ a particle resembling the verb, and the hāʾ is its noun. ﴿لا إِلهَ﴾ لا is the lā of generic negation, and إله is its noun; the clause is the khabar of أنه. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿أَنَا﴾ badal (substitute) from the position of لا and its noun. ﴿فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition). ﴿اعبدون﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya); its fāʿil [is the wāw], and its object is the deleted yāʾ; the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمنُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَلَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿سُبْحانَهُ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being سبح; the clause is parenthetical. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression. ﴿عِبادٌ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هم. ﴿مُكْرَمُونَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective). ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَسْبِقُونَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a naʿt. ﴿بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ the two are attached to يسبقونه. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ the two are attached to يعملون, and the clause يعملون is the khabar of هم; the clause ﴿هُمْ بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes.

daas-irab:28-29.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes. ﴿ما﴾ ما is relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَما خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is relative, conjoined to what precedes. ﴿خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ an adverb attached to the ṣila, and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negating. ﴿يَشْفَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a naʿt. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿لِمَنِ﴾ the lām is a preposition and من is a relative noun; the two are attached to يشفعون. ﴿ارْتَضى﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to مشفقون. ﴿مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate) of هم; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَقُلْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its fāʿil latent. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِنِّي إِلهٌ﴾ إن, its noun and its khabar; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the khabar. ﴿فَذلِكَ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis. ﴿ذلك﴾ mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿نَجْزِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of ذلك. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ the kāf is a preposition, and the demonstrative is in the position of the genitive; the two are attached to a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿نَجْزِي﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil omitted. [Translator's note: the source says "omitted" (محذوف); elsewhere it describes such a fāʿil as latent (mustatir).] ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من.

daas-irab:30-31.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation and the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لَمْ﴾ a particle of negation, jussive government and conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning]. ﴿يَرَ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ its noun. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) fills the place of the two objects of ير. ﴿كانَتا﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the alif is its noun. ﴿رَتْقاً﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause كانتا رتقا is the khabar of أن. ﴿فَفَتَقْناهُما﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿فتقناهما﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to كانتا. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنَ الْماءِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) جعلنا. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿حَيٍّ﴾ a naʿt (adjective). ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction and لا is negating. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿جَعَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَواسِيَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْ﴾ an accusative-governing particle. ﴿تَمِيدَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; أن and what follows it are, as an interpreted maṣdar, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to تميد. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to جعلنا. ﴿فِجاجاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿سُبُلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ لعل is a particle resembling the verb, and the hāʾ is its noun. ﴿يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لعل.

daas-irab:32-34.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿السَّماءَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿سَقْفاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مَحْفُوظاً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). [Translator's note: so in the source; محفوظا is ordinarily parsed as a naʿt (adjective) of سقفا.] ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and هم is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَنْ آياتِها﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) معرضون. ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate) of هم; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ khabar of هو. ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿اللَّيْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالنَّهارَ﴾ conjoined to الليل. ﴿وَالشَّمْسَ﴾ conjoined. ﴿وَالْقَمَرَ﴾ conjoined. ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي فَلَكٍ﴾ the two are attached to يسبحون; the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is a ḥāl. ﴿يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كل. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿جَعَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِبَشَرٍ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of بشر. ﴿الْخُلْدَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَفَإِنْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إن is a jussive-governing conditional particle. ﴿مِتَّ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَهُمُ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis. ﴿هم﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْخالِدُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

daas-irab:35-38.t: ﴿كُلُّ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ذائِقَةُ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿الْمَوْتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَنَبْلُوكُمْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive. ﴿نَبْلُوكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the kāf is its object. ﴿بِالشَّرِّ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) نبلوكم. ﴿وَالْخَيْرِ﴾ conjoined to الشر; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿وَإِلَيْنا﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ترجعون. ﴿تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is resumptive. ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial and conditional. ﴿رَآكَ﴾ a past verb and its object; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنْ﴾ negating. ﴿يَتَّخِذُونَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its first object. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿هُزُواً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَهذَا﴾ the hamza is for interrogation. ﴿هذَا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ khabar. ﴿يَذْكُرُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ṣila with no grammatical position. ﴿آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِذِكْرِ﴾ the two are attached to كافرون. ﴿الرَّحْمنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هُمْ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) of the first هم. ﴿كافِرُونَ﴾ their khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿خُلِقَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾ the two are attached to خلق. ﴿سَأُرِيكُمْ﴾ the sīn is for the future; an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, and its first object. ﴿آياتِي﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive. ﴿تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by deletion of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the deleted yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَتى﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb, attached to the fronted khabar; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿هذَا﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْوَعْدُ﴾ badal (substitute) from هذا. ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ إن is a jussive-governing conditional particle. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ khabar of كان; the clause كنتم is initial with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted.

daas-irab:39-40.t: ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, not jussive-governing. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil (agent). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿حِينَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَكُفُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ṣila. [Translator's note: so in the source; a clause after حين is ordinarily parsed as muḍāf ilayhi.] ﴿عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يكفون, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿النَّارَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; لا is negating. ﴿عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to يكفون. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. ﴿تَأْتِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; لا is negating. ﴿يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿رَدَّها﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar, and the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is conjoined.

daas-irab:41-43.t: ﴿وَلَقَدِ﴾ the wāw is resumptive. ﴿لَقَدِ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath. ﴿قد﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿اسْتُهْزِئَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿بِرُسُلٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun standing in the place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of رسل. ﴿فَحاقَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿حاق﴾ a past verb. ﴿بِالَّذِينَ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition. ﴿الذين﴾ a relative noun; the two are attached to حاق. ﴿سَخِرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to سخروا. ﴿ما﴾ ما is a relative noun, fāʿil. ﴿كانُوا﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its noun. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to يستهزئون. ﴿يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَنْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَكْلَؤُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar, and the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿بِاللَّيْلِ﴾ the two are attached to يكلؤكم. ﴿وَالنَّهارِ﴾ conjoined to الليل. ﴿مِنَ الرَّحْمنِ﴾ the two are attached to يكلؤهم [sic]. [Translator's note: the source writes يكلؤهم; the verb in the verse is يكلؤكم.] ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِ﴾ the two are attached to معرضون. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ khabar of هم. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿آلِهَةٌ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿تَمْنَعُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ دُونِنا﴾ the two are attached to تمنعهم; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿نَصْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is resumptive. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنَّا﴾ the two are attached to يصحبون; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar.

daas-irab:44-46.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿مَتَّعْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾ the hā is for calling attention (tanbīh); أولاء is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَآباءَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿آباءَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to هؤلاء, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) taking the genitive. ﴿طالَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) طال. ﴿الْعُمُرُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is for interrogation and the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَنَّا﴾ أن is a particle resembling the verb and نا is its noun; its original form is أننا, and the two nūns were assimilated. ﴿نَأْتِي﴾ an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; أنّا and what follows it fill the place of the two objects of يرون. ﴿نَنْقُصُها﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being نحن. ﴿مِنْ أَطْرافِها﴾ the two are attached to ننقصها; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَفَهُمُ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation and the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿هم﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْغالِبُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿أُنْذِرُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿بِالْوَحْيِ﴾ the two are attached to أنذركم. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَسْمَعُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿الصُّمُّ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الدُّعاءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial. ﴿ما﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿يُنْذَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ the lām paves the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam). ﴿إن﴾ a jussive-governing conditional particle. ﴿مَسَّتْهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object; it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿نَفْحَةٌ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ the two are attached to a naʿt (adjective) of نفحة. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath. ﴿يقولن﴾ an imperfect verb; the wāw, which is the fāʿil, was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ﴿يا وَيْلَنا﴾ يا is for the vocative or for calling attention. ﴿وَيْلَنا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied (muqaddar) verb. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ إن and its noun; its original form is إننا. ﴿كُنَّا﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿ظالِمِينَ﴾ khabar of كنا; the clause is the khabar of إن.

daas-irab:47-49.t: ﴿وَنَضَعُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿الْمَوازِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْقِسْطَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective). ﴿لِيَوْمِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) نضع. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿تُظْلَمُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿نَفْسٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional. ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿مِثْقالَ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿حَبَّةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾ the two are attached to a naʿt of حبة. ﴿أَتَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) with no grammatical position. ﴿بِها﴾ the two are attached to أتينا. ﴿وَكَفى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb. ﴿بِنا﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and نا is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. ﴿حاسِبِينَ﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿آتَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مُوسى﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَهارُونَ﴾ conjoined to موسى. ﴿الْفُرْقانَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَضِياءً﴾ conjoined to الفرقان. ﴿وَذِكْراً﴾ conjoined. ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ the two are attached to ذكرا. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a naʿt. ﴿يَخْشَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿رَبَّهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يخشون. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنَ السَّاعَةِ﴾ the two are attached to مشفقون. ﴿مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ khabar of هم; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:50-53.t: ﴿وَهذا﴾ the wāw is resumptive. ﴿هذا﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ذِكْرٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿مُبارَكٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective). ﴿أَنْزَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a naʿt. ﴿أَفَأَنْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation and the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿أنتم﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) منكرون. ﴿مُنْكِرُونَ﴾ khabar of أنتم; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the lām occurs in the response to the oath. ﴿قد﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿آتَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رُشْدَهُ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; كان and its noun. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to عالمين. ﴿عالِمِينَ﴾ khabar of كنا; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb attached to an omitted verb, اذكر. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, and its fāʿil is omitted; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). [Translator's note: the source says "omitted" (محذوف); the fāʿil is ordinarily called latent (mustatir).] ﴿لِأَبِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to قال. ﴿وَقَوْمِهِ﴾ conjoined to أبيه. ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿هذِهِ﴾ the hā is for calling attention (tanbīh). ﴿ذه﴾ khabar; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿التَّماثِيلُ﴾ badal (substitute) from the demonstrative. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a naʿt of التماثيل. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَها﴾ the two are attached to عاكفون. ﴿عاكِفُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَجَدْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿آباءَنا﴾ first mafʿūl bihi, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَها﴾ the two are attached to عابدين. ﴿عابِدِينَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl.

daas-irab:54-57.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath. ﴿قد﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis). ﴿وَآباؤُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to the noun of كان. ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ a naʿt (adjective); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَجِئْتَنا﴾ the hamza is for interrogation. ﴿جِئْتَنا﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to جئتنا; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنَ اللَّاعِبِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the khabar of أنت; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿رَبُّكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رَبُّ﴾ khabar. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات; the clause is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. [Translator's note: so in the source; the nominal clause is presumably meant as the maqūl al-qawl of قال.] ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a naʿt of رب, in the position of the nominative. ﴿فَطَرَهُنَّ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَأَنَا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿أَنَا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلى ذلِكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to الشاهدين; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿وَتَاللَّهِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿تَاللَّهِ﴾ the tāʾ is a particle of oath; the two are attached to the omitted أقسم. ﴿لَأَكِيدَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath. ﴿أكيدن﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, its fāʿil latent; the nūn has no grammatical position. ﴿أَصْنامَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: so in the source; the attached pronoun here is the kāf.] ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb attached to أكيدن. ﴿أَنْ﴾ an accusative-governing particle. ﴿تُوَلُّوا﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مُدْبِرِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); أن تولوا is, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:58-61.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿جعلهم﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿جُذاذاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿كَبِيراً﴾ excepted (mustathnā) by إلا. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of كبيرا. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ لعل and its noun. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to يرجعون, and the clause ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of لعل; the clause لعلهم is resumptive. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فَعَلَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar, and the mubtadaʾ and khabar are the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿هذا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِآلِهَتِنا﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ إن and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿من الظالمين﴾ the two are attached to the khabar of إن; the clause is resumptive. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿سَمِعْنا﴾ a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿فَتًى﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَذْكُرُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is a naʿt of فتى. ﴿يُقالُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to يقال. ﴿إِبْراهِيمُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَأْتُوا﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition). ﴿أتوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to فأتوا. ﴿عَلى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ لعل and its noun. ﴿يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لعل, and the clause لعل is resumptive.
