daas-irab:62-66.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَأَنْتَ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and أنت is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فَعَلْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate), and the clause ﴿أَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ﴾ is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿هذا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِآلِهَتِنا﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) فعلت. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿إِبْراهِيمُ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper noun, in the position of the accusative. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ﴾ a past verb, mafʿūl bihi and postponed fāʿil. ﴿هذا﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of كبيرهم. ﴿فَسْئَلُوهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition). ﴿اسألوهم﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كانُوا﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its noun; the clause ﴿يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ is its khabar, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted. ﴿فَرَجَعُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; a past verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to رجعوا. ﴿فَقالُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾ إن and its noun; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿أَنْتُمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is the khabar of إن. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction denoting delay. ﴿نُكِسُوا﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿والواو﴾ and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلى رُؤُسِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to نكسوا. ﴿لَقَدْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath. ﴿قد﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿عَلِمْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ negating the genus (nāfiya lil-jins). [Translator's note: so in the source; ما here is ordinarily parsed as the Ḥijāzī ما that acts like ليس; "its noun" and "its khabar" below refer to it.] ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾ the hā is for calling attention (tanbīh). ﴿أولاء﴾ its noun. ﴿يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is its khabar. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation and the fāʾ is a conjunction; an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ the two are attached to تعبدون. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَنْفَعُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَضُرُّكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:67-70.t: ﴿أُفٍّ﴾ a verbal noun with imperfect meaning (ism fiʿl muḍāriʿ); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلِما تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is a preposition, and ما is relative, in the position of the genitive; the two are conjoined to لكم, and the clause تعبدون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is for disapproving interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لا is negating. ﴿تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿قالُوا﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿حَرِّقُوهُ﴾ an imperative verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَانْصُرُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi and the mīm is for the plural. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿فاعِلِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate); كنتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being حرقوه وانصروا etc. ﴿قُلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿نارُ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite noun (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative. ﴿كُونِي بَرْداً﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, its noun and its khabar. ﴿وَسَلاماً﴾ conjoined to بردا; the clause يا نار.. is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿وَأَرادُوا بِهِ كَيْداً﴾ the clause of the verb, the fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi is conjoined to قالوا, and به: the two are attached to أرادوا. ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُمُ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and its first object; the clause is conjoined by the fāʾ. ﴿الْأَخْسَرِينَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:71-73.t: ﴿وَنَجَّيْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes. ﴿وَلُوطاً﴾ conjoined to the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of نجيناه. ﴿إِلَى الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the preceding verb. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun, a naʿt (adjective) in the position of the genitive. ﴿بارَكْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to باركنا. ﴿لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ the lām is a preposition, and العالمين is a genitive noun, genitive with the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; the two are attached to باركنا. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿وَهَبْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to the preceding verb. ﴿إِسْحاقَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). ﴿وَيَعْقُوبَ﴾ conjoined to إسحق. ﴿نافِلَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial) from يعقوب. ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and كلا is the fronted first mafʿūl bihi of جعلنا. ﴿جَعَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿صالِحِينَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَجَعَلْناهُمْ أَئِمَّةً﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb, its fāʿil and its two objects; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿يَهْدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a naʿt of أئمة. ﴿بِأَمْرِنا﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the preceding verb. ﴿فِعْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْخَيْراتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَإِقامَ﴾ conjoined to فعل. ﴿الصَّلاةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَإِيتاءَ الزَّكاةِ﴾ conjoined to فعل, and الزكاة is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَكانُوا لَنا عابِدِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; كان, its noun and its khabar (predicate); لنا: the two are attached to عابدين.

daas-irab:74-75.t: ﴿وَلُوطاً﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لوطا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned. ﴿آتَيْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first object; the clause is explicative (mufassira) with no grammatical position. ﴿حُكْماً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi of آتيناه. ﴿وَعِلْماً﴾ conjoined to حكما. ﴿وَنَجَّيْناهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes. ﴿مِنَ الْقَرْيَةِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) نجيناه. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun whose position is that of a naʿt (adjective) of القرية. ﴿كانَتْ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun omitted, its implied form being هي. ﴿تَعْمَلُ الْخَبائِثَ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil omitted, and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كان, and the clause كانت is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source says "omitted" (محذوف) for the noun of كانت and the fāʿil of تعمل; such pronouns are ordinarily called latent (mustatir).] ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ إن and its noun; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. ﴿كانُوا﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is the khabar of إن. ﴿قَوْمَ﴾ khabar of كانوا. ﴿سَوْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فاسِقِينَ﴾ a naʿt, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ. ﴿وَأَدْخَلْناهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿فِي رَحْمَتِنا﴾ the two are attached to أدخلناه. ﴿إِنَّهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ إن and its noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the khabar; the clause إن etc. is causal with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:76-77.t: ﴿وَنُوحاً﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and نوحا is conjoined to لوطا. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿نادى﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the shortened alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur); its fāʿil (agent) is omitted, its implied form being هو; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) نادى; قبل is an adverb indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording, not in meaning. ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) by the fāʾ to what precedes. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to استجبنا. ﴿فَنَجَّيْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَأَهْلَهُ﴾ conjoined to the object of نجيناه, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنَ الْكَرْبِ﴾ the two are attached to نجيناه. ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of الكرب. ﴿وَنَصَرْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿مِنَ الْقَوْمِ﴾ the two are attached to نصرناه. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of القوم. ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كذبوا, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ إن and its noun, and the mīm is for the plural; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿كانُوا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن. ﴿قَوْمَ﴾ khabar of كانوا. ﴿سَوْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأَغْرَقْناهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause أغرقناهم, made up of the verb, the fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), is conjoined by the fāʾ. ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in أغرقناهم, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.

daas-irab:78-80.t: ﴿وَداوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ﴾ conjoined to ونوحا. ﴿إِذْ يَحْكُمانِ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فِي الْحَرْثِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحكمان. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb attached to the preceding verb. ﴿نَفَشَتْ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to نفشت. ﴿غَنَمُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الْقَوْمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَ﴾ resumptive. ﴿كُنَّا﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿لِحُكْمِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to شاهدين; the clause is resumptive. ﴿شاهِدِينَ﴾ khabar (predicate), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿فَفَهَّمْناها سُلَيْمانَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; a past verb, its fāʿil and its two objects; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes. ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and [كلا is the] first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of آتينا. ﴿آتَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿حُكْماً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi of آتينا. ﴿وَعِلْماً﴾ conjoined to حكما; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَسَخَّرْنا﴾ the wāw is resumptive; a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb attached to سخرنا. ﴿داوُدَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, a diptote. ﴿الْجِبالَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of سخرنا. ﴿يُسَبِّحْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is joined to the nūn of the feminine plural, and the nūn is the fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الجبال. ﴿وَالطَّيْرَ﴾ conjoined to الجبال, or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿فاعِلِينَ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَعَلَّمْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿صَنْعَةَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَبُوسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of لبوس. ﴿لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām of causation (taʿlīl), its fāʿil latent (mustatir), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; أن and what follows it are, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of the genitive, [and with the lām] the two are attached to علمناه. ﴿مِنْ بَأْسِكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ شاكِرُونَ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, هل is an interrogative particle, أنتم is mubtadaʾ (subject) and شاكرون is khabar; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:81-82.t: ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمانَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being سخرنا. ﴿الرِّيحَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the omitted verb. ﴿عاصِفَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial) from الريح. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is a second ḥāl. ﴿بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿إِلى الْأَرْضِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun whose position is the genitive, as a naʿt (adjective). ﴿بارَكْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the verb before them. ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ the two are attached to the khabar (predicate) after them. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عالِمِينَ﴾ khabar, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿وَمِنَ الشَّياطِينِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being وسخرنا. ﴿مِنَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the omitted verb سخرنا; or it is in the position of the nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and من الشياطين is attached to a fronted khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. [Translator's note: the parsed word is the relative noun ﴿مَنْ﴾ of the verse; the source vocalises it مِنَ.] ﴿يَغُوصُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ṣila with no grammatical position. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to the preceding verb. ﴿وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًا﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined. ﴿دُونَ﴾ an adverb attached to a naʿt of عملا. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to حافظين. ﴿حافِظِينَ﴾ the khabar of كنا, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:83-85.t: ﴿وَأَيُّوبَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and أيوب is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb اذكر. ﴿نادى﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause نادى is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رَبَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of نادى, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَنِّي﴾ أن and its noun. ﴿مَسَّنِيَ﴾ a past verb; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is a fronted mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الضُّرُّ﴾ postponed fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن. ﴿وَأَنْتَ أَرْحَمُ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl, [then] mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and استجبنا is a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to استجبنا. ﴿فَكَشَفْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ما﴾ relative, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the two are attached to the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَهْلَهُ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِثْلَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to أهله. ﴿مَعَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنا﴾ the two are attached to a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة. ﴿وَذِكْرى﴾ conjoined to رحمة. ﴿لِلْعابِدِينَ﴾ the two are attached to ذكرى. ﴿وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ﴾ conjoined to the prophets already mentioned. ﴿وَإِسْماعِيلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر. ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:86-88.t: ﴿وَأَدْخَلْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes. ﴿فِي رَحْمَتِنا﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ إن and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the khabar (predicate) of إن; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. ﴿وَذَا النُّونِ﴾ conjoined to the prophets already mentioned, or ذا is the mafʿūl bihi of the verb اذكر, accusative (manṣūb) with the alif because it is one of the five nouns; النون, meaning "the whale", is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time attached to the implied (muqaddar) verb اذكر. ﴿ذَهَبَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُغاضِباً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the latent fāʿil. ﴿فَظَنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy أنّ, its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَنْ﴾ a particle of negation, accusative government and futurity. ﴿نَقْدِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by لن, its fāʿil latent. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ the two are attached to نقدر; أن and what follows it fill the place of the two objects of ظن. ﴿فَنادى﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied fatḥa on the alif, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being هو; the clause is conjoined by the fāʾ to what precedes. ﴿فِي الظُّلُماتِ﴾ the two are attached to نادى. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a particle resembling the verb, lightened from the heavy أنّ, its noun being the pronoun of the matter, its implied form being أنه. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الله﴾ the Name of Majesty, badal (substitute); the clause is the khabar of أن. ﴿سُبْحانَكَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being أسبح, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause reinforces the preceding clause. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ إن and its noun. ﴿كُنْتُ﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the khabar of كنت; the clause is the khabar of إني, and the clause إني is causal with no grammatical position. ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَنَجَّيْناهُ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنَ الْغَمِّ﴾ the two are attached to نجيناه. ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the kāf is a preposition and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive; the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of a mafʿūl muṭlaq; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿نُنْجِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness, its fāʿil latent. ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:89-91.t: ﴿وَزَكَرِيَّا﴾ conjoined to what precedes, or the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the omitted verb اذكر. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿نادى﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رَبَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), accusative (manṣūb), the vocative particle having been omitted; the sign of its accusative is an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, which was deleted for lightness, and the deleted yāʾ of the speaker is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا﴾ prohibitive, used for supplication. ﴿تَذَرْنِي﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَرْداً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative; the preceding clauses are in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech) of the omitted verb قال, its implied form being قال رب etc. ﴿وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), [then] mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿الْوارِثِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) استجبنا. ﴿وَوَهَبْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُ﴾ the two are attached to وهبنا. ﴿يَحْيى﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative with an implied fatḥa on the alif; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) by the wāw, and likewise ﴿وَأَصْلَحْنا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ﴾. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ إن and its noun; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. ﴿كانُوا﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is the khabar of إن. ﴿يُسارِعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كان. ﴿فِي الْخَيْراتِ﴾ the two are attached to يسارعون. ﴿وَيَدْعُونَنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; an imperfect verb, nominative by retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and نا is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَغَباً وَرَهَباً﴾ two ḥāls, or two mafʿūls li-ajlihi (objects of purpose). ﴿وَكانُوا﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿لَنا﴾ the two are attached to the postponed khabar. ﴿خاشِعِينَ﴾ khabar, accusative with the yāʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَالَّتِي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the omitted verb اذكر; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها﴾ a past verb, the tāʾ being for the feminine, its fāʿil latent, and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿فَنَفَخْنا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to نفخنا. ﴿مِنْ رُوحِنا﴾ the two are attached to نفخنا, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَجَعَلْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object. ﴿وَابْنَها﴾ conjoined to the hāʾ in جعلناها, or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). ﴿آيَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ the lām is a preposition, and العالمين is a genitive noun, genitive with the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined to what precedes.

daas-irab:92-95.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿هذِهِ﴾ the hāʾ is for calling attention (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as the noun of إن. ﴿أُمَّتُكُمْ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿أُمَّةً﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a badal (substitute) from هذه. ﴿واحِدَةً﴾ a naʿt (adjective). ﴿وَأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) by the wāw. ﴿فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اعبدون is an imperative verb, the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and the yāʾ of the speaker, deleted following the orthography of the Muṣḥaf, is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَتَقَطَّعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَمْرَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, in the sense of "they split up their affair". ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb تقطعوا, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَيْنا﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to راجعون. ﴿راجِعُونَ﴾ khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is a ḥāl or resumptive. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَعْمَلْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm); it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ the two are attached to يعمل. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هو is mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, and لا is negating, operating like إنّ. ﴿كُفْرانَ﴾ its noun. ﴿لِسَعْيِهِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted khabar of لا. ﴿وَإِنَّا لَهُ كاتِبُونَ﴾ إن, its noun and its khabar, and له: the two are attached to the khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَحَرامٌ﴾ fronted khabar. ﴿عَلى قَرْيَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to حرام. ﴿أَهْلَكْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a naʿt of قرية. ﴿أَنَّهُمْ لا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ أن, and the hāʾ is its noun; لا is negating, and يرجعون is an imperfect verb, the wāw being its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of أن, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أنّ and what follows it is the postponed mubtadaʾ.

daas-irab:96-97.t: ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) taking the genitive. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb for future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [verb], its implied form being قالوا يا ويلنا. ﴿فُتِحَتْ﴾ a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿يَأْجُوجُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿وَمَأْجُوجُ﴾ conjoined to it; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl, and هم is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to ينسلون. ﴿حَدَبٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَنْسِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate), and the clause هم etc. is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَاقْتَرَبَ الْوَعْدُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes. ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of الوعد. ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is the one of surprise (fujāʾiyya); it enters upon the nominal clause and has no grammatical position. ﴿هِيَ شاخِصَةٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿أَبْصارُ﴾ fāʿil of شاخصة. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿يا﴾ vocative. ﴿وَيْلَنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), in a genitive construct (muḍāf), and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech) of an omitted verb, its implied form being قالوا يا ويلنا. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كُنَّا﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿فِي غَفْلَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a preposition. ﴿هذا﴾ the hā is for calling attention (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive; the two are attached to غفلة. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿كُنَّا﴾ كان and its noun. ﴿ظالِمِينَ﴾ khabar of كان, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is the omitted maqūl al-qawl.

daas-irab:98-101.t: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾ إن and its noun, and the mīm is for the plural. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is relative, conjoined to the kāf. ﴿تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ omitted in تعبدونه. ﴿حَصَبُ﴾ khabar (predicate) of إن, and its clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa because it is a diptote. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَها﴾ the two are attached to the postponed khabar. ﴿وارِدُونَ﴾ khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle, not jussive-governing. ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾ the hā is for calling attention (tanbīh), and أولاء is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of the nominative as the noun of كان. ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ khabar; the clause is initial with no grammatical position. ﴿ما﴾ negating. ﴿وَرَدُوها﴾ a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَكُلٌّ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the postponed khabar. ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾ khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿زَفِيرٌ﴾ postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; هم is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to يسمعون. ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ لا is negating, and يسمعون is an imperfect verb, nominative by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, the noun of إن. ﴿سَبَقَتْ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ and ﴿مِنَّا﴾ both are attached to the verb. ﴿الْحُسْنى﴾ fāʿil, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur). ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿عَنْها﴾ the two are attached to مبعدون. ﴿مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إن.

daas-irab:102-104.t: ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿حَسِيسَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ها is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); the clause is a second khabar (predicate) of إن, or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in مبعدون. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and هم is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي﴾ a preposition. ﴿مَا﴾ relative; the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb after them. [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb after them is the ṣila, and the attachment is presumably to خالدون.] ﴿اشْتَهَتْ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and the mīm is for the plural; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾ khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ﴾ لا is negating; an imperfect verb and its object, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: so in the source; the hāʾ here is the verb's object, as the source itself has just said.] ﴿الْفَزَعُ﴾ postponed fāʿil. ﴿الْأَكْبَرُ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of الفزع; the clause is a badal (substitute) from the preceding clause, or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿وَتَتَلَقَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the hāʾ is its fronted object and الملائكة its postponed fāʿil; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to what precedes. ﴿هذا يَوْمُكُمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech) of the omitted verb يقولون. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun, a naʿt of يوم, in the position of the nominative. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ كان and its noun; the clause is a ṣila with no grammatical position. ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of كنتم. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to the omitted verb اذكر. ﴿نَطْوِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness, its fāʿil latent; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿السَّماءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَطَيِّ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the implied form being طيا. ﴿السِّجِلِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِلْكُتُبِ﴾ the two are attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun). ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ relative or maṣdariyya. ﴿بَدَأْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَوَّلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿خَلْقٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿نُعِيدُهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, its fāʿil latent. ﴿وَعْداً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb. ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ the two are attached to وعدا. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ إن and its noun. ﴿كُنَّا﴾ كان and its noun; the clause كنا etc. is the khabar of إن, and إن with its noun and khabar is a resumptive clause. ﴿فاعِلِينَ﴾ the khabar of كان, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.

daas-irab:105-108.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿كَتَبْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِي الزَّبُورِ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) كتبنا; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the response to an oath. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the two are attached to the preceding verb. ﴿الذِّكْرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَنَّ الْأَرْضَ﴾ أن and its noun; its clause is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَرِثُها﴾ an imperfect verb and its object. ﴿عِبادِيَ﴾ fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن. ﴿الصَّالِحُونَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿فِي هذا﴾ ذا is a demonstrative; the two are attached to the omitted fronted khabar of إن. ﴿لَبَلاغاً﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and بلاغا is the postponed noun of إن. ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ the two are attached to بلاغا. ﴿عابِدِينَ﴾ a naʿt of قوم, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive and ما is negating. ﴿أَرْسَلْناكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ the two are attached to رحمة. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿يُوحى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ the two are attached to يوحى. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining and the restrained. ﴿إِلهُكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلهٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿واحِدٌ﴾ a naʿt of إله; the clause أنما إلهكم إله is, as an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يوحى. [Translator's note: the source heads this word ﴿إِنَّما﴾, but the verse reads ﴿أَنَّما﴾, as its own analysis (أنما … in the position of nāʾib fāʿil) assumes.] ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; هل is an interrogative particle. ﴿أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:109-112.t: ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is a jussive-governing conditional particle. ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif, which was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis, and قل is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿آذَنْتُكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿عَلى سَواءٍ﴾ the two (preposition and its genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) آذنتكم. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and إن is a particle of negation. ﴿أَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness, its fāʿil latent; the clause is resumptive or a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَقَرِيبٌ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation. ﴿قَرِيبٌ﴾ fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿بَعِيدٌ﴾ conjoined to قريب. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of the nominative as postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl of أدري. [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause is ordinarily described as the object of أدري, whose operation is suspended.] ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ إن and its noun. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿الْجَهْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar. ﴿مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl from الجهر. ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent; the clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَكْتُمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and إن is negating. ﴿أَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative with an implied ḍamma on the yāʾ owing to heaviness, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ لعل, its noun and its khabar. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to فتنة or to a naʿt (adjective) of it. ﴿وَمَتاعٌ﴾ conjoined to فتنة. ﴿إِلى حِينٍ﴾ the two are attached to متاع; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of أدري. ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle; it is annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿احْكُمْ﴾ a verb of supplication, its fāʿil omitted. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to احكم. ﴿وَرَبُّنَا الرَّحْمنُ الْمُسْتَعانُ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلى ما﴾ ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by على, and the two are attached to المستعان. ﴿تَصِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila.

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النَّجْوَى): secret talk; it is a noun from al-tanājī (confiding with one another), and it is only ever hidden. In al-Qāmūs: "It is a description by a maṣdar (verbal noun), in which singular and plural are alike; one says: هم نجوى (they are [people in] secret counsel)."
(أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ): jumbled things one sees in sleep; its discussion has preceded.

* I'rab:
(اقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مُعْرِضُونَ): اقترب is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; للناس is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اقترب. It may also be an emphasis of the ascription of the reckoning to them, as when you say أزف للحي رحيلهم ("their departure has drawn near for the tribe"); the original is أزف رحيل الحي, then أزف للحي الرحيل, then أزف للحي رحيلهم. حسابهم is the fāʿil (agent) of اقترب, because everything that is coming is near, however long the interval. The wāw is of the ḥāl (circumstantial); هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), في غفلة is the khabar (predicate), and معرضون is a second khabar. (ما يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ): the clause gives the cause of the preceding clause, so it has no grammatical position. ما is negative; يأتيهم is an imperfect verb, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, because it is preceded by negation; ذكر is genitive in form and nominative in position as the fāʿil; من ربهم is an adjective (naʿt) of ذكر, and محدث is a second adjective. من ربهم may also be attached to يأتيهم, or to an omitted ḥāl of ذكر, since it is described by محدث. إلا is a particle of restriction, because the exception is emptied (mufarragh). The clause استمعوه is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the object of يأتيهم, with قد implied. وهم: the wāw is circumstantial, هم is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يلعبون is the khabar of هم; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of استمعوه. Moreover, the description of the reminder (al-dhikr) as "new" (muḥdath) has been taken as proof that the Qur'an is originated (muḥdath), since the reminder here is the Qur'an. The answer given is that there is no dispute about the originatedness of what is composed of sounds and letters, since it is renewed in being sent down, so the meaning is "its sending down is new"; the dispute concerns only the inner speech (al-kalām al-nafsī).
(لاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا هَلْ هذا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ): لاهية is likewise a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يلعبون, so it is an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl; it may also be a ḥāl of the fāʿil of استمعوه, in which case the two ḥāls are consecutive (mutarādifa), since a ḥāl may be multiple. قلوبهم is the fāʿil of لاهية. أسروا is a verb and its fāʿil, and النجوى is the mafʿūl bihi. الذين is a badal (substitute) of the wāw of وأسروا النجوى, to indicate that they are the ones branded with the gross wrongdoing they committed; more on the parsing of this word will come in the section on benefits. The clause ظلموا is the ṣila (relative clause). هل is an interrogative particle, هذا is a mubtadaʾ, إلا is a particle of restriction, and بشر is the khabar; مثلكم is an adjective. The interrogative clause is in the position of accusative as a badal of النجوى, since it serves as its explanation. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be in the position of accusative as the object of an omitted verb of saying; it may also be in the position of accusative as the reported content of النجوى, since that has the meaning of saying. I see nothing to prevent it [Translator's note: the source has «من أتكون», a misprint for «من أن تكون»] from being a clause with no grammatical position, because it is explicative. (أَفَتَأْتُونَ السِّحْرَ وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ): the preceding views apply to this clause as well. The hamza is interrogative, and the fāʾ is a conjunction onto something implied; تأتون السحر is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. The wāw is of the ḥāl; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause تبصرون is the khabar; the clause وأنتم تبصرون is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تأتون, reinforcing the denial. (قالَ رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ الْقَوْلَ فِي السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): ربي is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يعلم القول is the khabar; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). في السماء والأرض is attached to an omitted ḥāl of القول, or to يعلم. وهو: the wāw is a conjunction, هو is a mubtadaʾ, and السميع العليم are two khabars of هو; what they are attached to is omitted because it is known, i.e. "the One who hears what they kept secret, and knows it".
(بَلْ قالُوا أَضْغاثُ أَحْلامٍ بَلِ افْتَراهُ بَلْ هُوَ شاعِرٌ): they turned away from their saying "it is magic" and said "it is jumbled dreams". So أضغاث أحلام is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of قالوا. بل افتراه: then they turned away from that and said "he invented it"; افتراه is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. Then they turned away again and said هو شاعر, a mubtadaʾ and a khabar. (فَلْيَأْتِنا بِآيَةٍ كَما أُرْسِلَ الْأَوَّلُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it discloses an implied condition, as though it were said: "and if it is not as we said, then let him bring us". The lām is the lām of command; يأت is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "he"; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi. The kāf [of كما] may be an adjective of آية, i.e. "being like the sign with which the former ones were sent", in which case ما is a relative noun; it may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, with ما maṣdariyya, i.e. "let him bring us a sign, a bringing like the sending of the former ones". [Translator's note: the source says «كما يجوز في الكاف» ("as it is also permissible for the kāf"), though no preceding alternative for the kāf is given; translated as written.]

* Benefits:
The saying of the Exalted «وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا». Abū al-Baqāʾ said:
"Regarding الذين ظلموا, there are three views on its position. The first: nominative, and in it there are four views:
a- That it is a badal of the wāw in وأسروا.
b- That it is the fāʿil, the wāw being a particle marking plurality, not a noun.
c- That it is a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being هل هذا, the implied sense being: 'they say: is this...?'
d- That it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. 'they are those who did wrong'.
The second: that it is accusative by an implied أعني ('I mean').
The third: that it is genitive as an adjective of الناس."
It is well known that the verb must remain in the singular form with its fāʿil, even if [the fāʿil] is dual or plural. Ibn Mālik said:
وجرد الفعل إذا ما أسندا ... لاثنين أو جمع كفاز الشهدا
(Strip the verb [of dual/plural markers] when it is ascribed to two or to a plural, as in فاز الشهدا "the martyrs have won".)
except in a weak dialect of some Arabs, in which the verb agrees with the fāʿil. The Basrans reported it from Ṭayyiʾ, and some reported it from Azd Shanūʾa [Translator's note: the source prints «ازدشنوءة»], e.g. ضربوني قومك ("your people struck me"), ضربنني نسوتك ("your women struck me") and ضرباني أخواك ("your two brothers struck me"). In the hadith: «أو مخرجيّ هم» ("Will they drive me out?"). And ʿAmr ibn Milqaṭ, the pre-Islamic poet, said:
ألفيتا عيناك عند القفا ... أولى فأولى لك ذا واقيه
(Your two eyes were found at the nape of your neck — woe upon woe to you, O you who seek protection!)
ألفيتا, in the passive, is a past verb and عيناك is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); so the verb received the dual marker even though it is ascribed to an overt noun, and the nāʾib fāʿil is like the fāʿil. عند is an adverb meaning "near", attached to ألفيتا. ذا واقية is a ḥāl of the muḍāf ilayhi, namely the kāf; واقية is a maṣdar meaning protection (wiqāya), like كاذبة, a maṣdar meaning lying. أولى فأولى لك is an imprecation, i.e. "may what will destroy you come near you". Al-ʿAynī said: "If you ask: what is the grammatical position of أولى? I say: it may be in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being 'my prayer [against you] is أولى لك'; فأولى لك is conjoined to the first أولى, repeated for emphasis." Abū al-Baqāʾ said in parsing أولى لك فأولى: there are two views on it. One is that it is [on the pattern] faʿlā, its alif being for attachment (ilḥāq), not for the feminine; the other is that it is afʿal. On both views it is [non-tanwīned] here, and that is why it was not given tanwīn; this is indicated by what Abū Zayd reported in al-Nawādir: هي أولاة with tāʾ [Translator's note: the source prints «أولات»]. It is a diptote because it has become a proper name for the threat, like a man named Aḥmad. On this view أولى is a mubtadaʾ and لك the khabar. The second is that it is an indeclinable verbal noun (ism fiʿl), meaning "woe to you, evil after evil", with لك for clarification. In this verse he describes a man who, when the battle grows fierce, turns to look behind him for fear of being pursued, so that his eyes are found at the back of his neck from the intensity of turning. And Abū Firās said:
تنج الربيع محاسنا ... ألقحنها غر السحائب
(Spring brings forth beauties, which the bright clouds impregnated.) [Translator's note: the verb تنج, with the feminine plural agreement in ألقحنها, illustrates the same dialect; the source prints the line this way.]
Abū Firās is one of the post-classical poets (muwalladūn), and the purpose in [citing] his words is illustration, not evidentiary citation (istishhād).
Shaykh Muṣṭafā al-Ghalāyīnī held a fine opinion, and we shall cite his text: "Whatever of this occurs in eloquent speech, the overt noun is parsed as a badal of the pronoun — and on this basis is the saying of the Exalted (وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا) — or the overt noun is parsed as a mubtadaʾ and the clause before it as a fronted khabar, or it is parsed as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, as though, after His saying وأسروا النجوى, it were asked: 'Who kept it secret?' and the reply were: 'Those who did wrong kept it secret.' This is the correct view, and it applies only where the context calls for implying an interrogative statement, as you see in the noble verse." We reckon that the matter has been discussed sufficiently, so what has preceded is enough for us.

dervis-irab:6-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قَصَمْنا): qaṣm is more intense than breaking (kasr). In al-Qāmūs: "qaṣama, of the pattern ṣaraba [Translator's note: so in the source, «صرب», evidently for ḍaraba «ضرب»], qaṣman al-shayʾ: he broke it; qaṣama al-rajul: he destroyed him; and one says: qaṣama Allāh ẓahr al-ẓālim, i.e. He brought calamity down upon him." The qāf together with the ṣād as the first and second radicals of a word holds a wonderful secret: they indicate breaking, effacing and destroying. Thus they say qaṣaba al-shāh, meaning he cut the sheep into pieces, limb by limb; from it the butcher is called al-qaṣṣāb, i.e. the slaughterer. Al-qaṣṣāba is the feminine of al-qaṣṣāb, and it has another meaning, namely what we today call "the nāy", i.e. a reed blown into for singing. From one of the Arabs: "I composed some verses, and Ḥakam al-Wādī sang them; by Allah, he did not move a qaṣṣāba with them but that I feared the Fire, so I gave up composing poetry" — and it is the string [Translator's note: so in the source]; and nafakha fī al-qaṣṣāba: in the pipe (mizmār). Aqṣadathu al-maniyya: death destroyed him; from it qaṣada al-rajul: he came to him and headed in his direction. Qaṣartuhu: I confined him; qaṣartu nafsī ʿalā hādhā al-amr when you do not aspire to anything else; qaṣartu ṭarfī: I did not raise my glance to what is improper; and hunna qāṣirāt al-ṭarf: they restrict it to their husbands. Qaṣṣa al-shaʿr wa-l-rīsh (he clipped hair and feathers) and qaṣṣaṣahu are well known, and a wing is maqṣūṣ and muqaṣṣaṣ. Qaṣaʿa al-ṣuʾāb bayna ẓufrayhi: he killed the nit between his two nails; qaṣaʿat al-raḥā al-ḥabb: the mill crushed the grain; and a ṣabī qaṣīʿ is a stunted boy who does not grow. Qaṣafa al-qanāt wa-l-ʿūd: he broke the spear-shaft and the stick; qaṣafa ẓahrahu, and a man is maqṣūf; the common people say to someone they curse "yā maqṣūf", and it is eloquent Arabic with nothing wrong in it. A wind blew and broke (qaṣafat) the ship; and a stick that is qaṣif: quick to break. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
تميم تمنّى الحرب ما لم ألاقها ... وهم قصف العيدان في الحرب خورها
(Tamīm long for war as long as I have not met them, yet in war they are brittle sticks, feeble.)
Qaṣalahu: he cut it off quickly (qaṭʿan wa-ḥayyan); a sword is qāṣil, qaṣṣāl and miqṣal; qaṣala farasahu yaqṣiluhu: he fed his horse green fodder (al-qaṣīl); from it is al-miqṣala (the guillotine), an instrument of execution consisting of a blade that falls upon the head of the criminal and cuts it off. Qaṣā yaqṣū qaṣwan, quṣuwwan, qaṣan and qaṣāʾan al-rajul: he went far away; and in farness there is an allusion to destruction, because it too is a going far.
(أُتْرِفْتُمْ): you were given ease of a comfortable life and a soft condition; al-itrāf is to make one insolent through blessing.

* I'rab:
(ما آمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْناها أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ): ما is negative; آمنت is a past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine; the clause is resumptive, brought to affirm their disbelief and to deem their believing far-fetched. قبلهم is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنت; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; قرية is genitive in form and in position the fāʿil (agent) of آمنت; the clause أهلكناها is an adjective (naʿt) of قرية. What is meant by the town is its people, as will come in the section on rhetoric. أفهم: the hamza is for the interrogative of denial, the fāʾ is a conjunction, هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يؤمنون is the khabar (predicate). (وَما أَرْسَلْنا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, أرسلنا is a past verb and its fāʿil, إلا is a particle of restriction, رجالا is the object of أرسلنا, and the clause نوحي إليهم is an adjective of رجالا; the imperfect form is used to narrate a past state. (فَسْئَلُوا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of an implied condition); اسألوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and أهل الذكر is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause لا تعلمون is its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa. (وَما جَعَلْناهُمْ جَسَداً لا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ وَما كانُوا خالِدِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, جعلناهم is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and جسدا is a second object if جعل has the sense of "making into" (taṣyīr); if it has the sense of creating, then جسدا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) interpreted as a derived word, i.e. "taking nourishment". The clause لا يأكلون الطعام is in the position of accusative as an adjective of جسدا. جسد is singular but the plural is meant; it was made singular only to include the genus in general, because a body must have nourishment. The wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, and كانوا خالدين is kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to لا يأكلون. (ثُمَّ صَدَقْناهُمُ الْوَعْدَ فَأَنْجَيْناهُمْ وَمَنْ نَشاءُ وَأَهْلَكْنَا الْمُسْرِفِينَ): ثم is a conjunction; صدقناهم is a verb, its fāʿil and its object; الوعد is accusative by removal of the preposition, because صدق is transitive to two objects, to the second of them through a preposition, the original being في الوعد. فأنجيناهم is conjoined to صدقناهم; ومن نشاء is conjoined to the hāʾ, and the clause نشاء is the ṣila (relative clause); وأهلكنا المسرفين is conjoined to أنجيناهم, and المسرفين is the mafʿūl bihi. (لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكُمْ كِتاباً فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): the lām is in reply to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of verification; أنزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; إليكم is attached to أنزلنا; كتابا is the mafʿūl bihi; فيه is a fronted khabar and ذكركم a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is an adjective of كتابا. The meaning of فيه ذكركم will come in the section on benefits. The hamza is for the interrogative of denial and rebuke, and the fāʾ is a conjunction onto something implied that the speech extends over, i.e. "Do you not reflect, so that you understand nothing of the things mentioned to you?" (وَكَمْ قَصَمْنا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ كانَتْ ظالِمَةً وَأَنْشَأْنا بَعْدَها قَوْماً آخَرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, or resumptive, brought to cite as an example the nations that perished before them. كم is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, a fronted mafʿūl bihi of قصمنا; من قرية is the tamyīz (specification) of the predicative kam, genitive by من, as has preceded. The clause كانت ظالمة is an adjective of قرية, the town meaning its people; كانت ظالمة is kāna, its latent (mustatir) noun and its khabar. أنشأنا is conjoined to قصمنا; بعدها is an adverb attached to أنشأنا; قوما is the mafʿūl bihi, and آخرين is an adjective of قوما. (فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوا بَأْسَنا إِذا هُمْ مِنْها يَرْكُضُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is a temporal adverb meaning "when", or a linking [particle]; إذا is the إذا of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya), and the discussion of it and the disagreement over it have preceded in full. هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يركضون its khabar; منها is attached to يركضون. Some have taken this verse as proof that لما is a particle; Ibn Hishām called it "linking" (rābiṭa) because, if parsed as an adverb meaning "when", it would have nothing governing it. We hold that the meaning of surprise indicated by إذا is what governs it. More discussion of لما will come in the section on benefits.
(لا تَرْكُضُوا وَارْجِعُوا إِلى ما أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَساكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْئَلُونَ): لا is prohibitive; تركضوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. The clause لا تركضوا is the object of an omitted verb of saying. There is disagreement about who said it: it is said they were the angels, and it is said they were those of the believers who were present; this saying is, of course, by way of mocking them. ارجعوا is an imperative verb conjoined to لا تركضوا; إلى ما is attached to ارجعوا; the clause أترفتم is the ṣila, and فيه is attached to أترفتم; مساكنكم, in the genitive, is conjoined to ما. لعلكم تسألون: laʿalla, its noun and its khabar. The hope here is mockery of them and derision of what they used to think of themselves, that they were the expected source of generosity and the dawning-place of liberality. The meaning is: "Return to your luxury and your dwellings; perhaps you will be asked for something of your worldly goods, according to how you imagine yourselves to be people of bounty and giving, whom people ask in misfortunes and calamities, summon for grave matters and consult on difficult problems." More on this delightful discussion will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- Synecdoche (al-majāz al-mursal) in His saying «قرية», since what is meant is its people; examples of this have preceded many times.
2- Derision (al-tahakkum) in His saying «وَارْجِعُوا إِلى ما أُتْرِفْتُمْ فِيهِ وَمَساكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْئَلُونَ». We have alluded to what is meant by this derision, and here we add two important possibilities arising from it:
a- That they were truly generous, bestowing gifts and stretching out their hands with presents, but they did so to be seen by people and to gain fame and praise. In that there is what pain and anguish there is, since they see that what they spent and gave was nothing but an increase in their torment and a deepening of their punishment.
b- That they were misers who hated giving and turned away whoever came seeking rain from the clouds of their palms and trying to milk the udders of their bounty; so this was said to them to add pain upon pain and anguish upon anguish.

* Benefits:
1- His saying «كِتاباً فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ»:
i.e. in it is what calls for praise of you, since it was sent down in your language, in your midst, and upon a messenger from among you. It is also said: in it is what you seek of good repute, far-reaching fame and fine report. It is also said: in it is admonition for you and guidance to what benefits you in your religion and your worldly life. All of that is possible.

2- A discussion of لما:
لما occurs in Arabic in three ways:

The first:
That it is specific to the imperfect verb, making it jussive, negating it and turning it to the past, like «لم», except that it differs from it in five matters:
1- It is not joined to a conditional particle; one does not say إن لما تقم, but one says إن لم تقم.
2- What it negates remains negated continuously up to the present, whereas what لم negates may be either continuous or discontinued, as in «لَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْئاً مَذْكُوراً». For this reason you may say لم يكن ثم كان ("it was not, then it was"), but you may not say لما يكن ثم كان.
3- What لما negates is usually close to the present, unlike what لم negates.
4- What لما negates is expected to come about, unlike what لم negates.
5- What لما negates may be omitted when there is an indication, as in the saying «فجئت قبورهم بدءا ولما» ("I came to their graves a chief, though I was not yet"), i.e. ولما أكن بدءا قبل ذلك, "and I had not been a chief (بدء) before that", i.e. a lord. But it is not permissible to say «وصلت إلى حمص ولم», meaning "and I did not enter it".

The second:
That it is specific to the past verb, requiring two clauses, the second of which came about upon the existence of the first, e.g. لما جاءني أكرمته ("when he came to me, I honoured him"). It is called a particle of existence due to existence; some say of necessity due to necessity. It is also said to be an adverb for an act that occurred because of the occurrence of another; and a group said it is an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīn).

The third:
That it is a particle of exception meaning إلا; it then enters upon the nominal clause, e.g. «إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ», according to those who read the mīm with shadda; and upon a verb that is past in form but not in meaning, e.g. أنشدك الله لما فعلت ("I adjure you by Allah, do it"), i.e. "I ask of you nothing but your doing it".

dervis-irab:14-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَصِيداً): faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), in which the singular and others are alike; its rule will come in the section on benefits. It is harvested crops.
(خامِدِينَ): one says khamadat al-nār and hamadat, each of them of the pattern dakhala; but the first denotes the dying down of its flame while the embers remain, and the second denotes its going out completely.
(لَهْواً): in al-Miṣbāḥ: "Lahw is well known. The people of Najd say lahawtu ʿanhu alhū luhiyyan, the original being on the pattern fuʿūl, of the pattern qaʿada; and the people of al-ʿĀliya say lahītu ʿanhu alhā, of the pattern taʿiba, and its meaning is forgetting and leaving. Lahawtu bihi lahwan, of the pattern qatala: I became fond of it, too. Al-Ṭurṭūshī said: the root meaning of lahw is relieving the soul with what wisdom does not require. Alhānī al-shayʾ, with the alif: the thing occupied me." End quote.
In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: "Lahā lahwan: he played, like iltahā; alhāhu dhālika (that distracted him); al-malāhī are its instruments (of amusement); talāhā bi-dhāka; al-uhlūwa, al-uhliyya and al-tilhiya are what one amuses oneself with. Lahat al-marʾa ilā ḥadīthihi lahwan and luhuwwan: she took pleasure in his talk and it pleased her. Al-lahwa is the woman one amuses oneself with, like al-lahw. With ḍamma and fatḥa [al-luhwa/al-lahwa]: what you throw into the mouth of the millstone; and a gift, or the best and most abundant of gifts, like al-luhya; and a handful of wealth, or a thousand dīnārs or dirhams, nothing else. Lahiya bihi, like raḍiya: he loved it; and [lahiya] ʿanhu: he forgot it, was heedless of it and ceased mentioning it — all of these like daʿā, lahyan and lahayānan." The commentator on al-Qāmūs said: "His saying 'lahā lahwan: he played' implies that the two are identical, but a group distinguished between them. It is said that they share in being occupation with what is of no concern, whether forbidden or not; and it is said that lahw is absolutely more general, so listening to musical instruments is lahw but not laʿib (play)." Al-Jawharī said: lahw is sometimes used as a euphemism for intercourse, and this is indicated by the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
ألا زعمت بسباسة اليوم أنني ... كبرت وان لا يحسن اللهو أمثالي
(Basbāsa claimed today that I have grown old, and that men like me are no good at dalliance.)
(فَيَدْمَغُهُ): so it does away with it; its pattern is qaṭaʿa. In al-Qāmūs: damaghahu: he overpowered it; damagha al-ḥaqq bi-l-bāṭil [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense required is "the truth crushed falsehood"]: it nullified and effaced it. Details of that will come in the section on rhetoric.
(يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ): they grow weary and tired. One says istaḥsara al-baʿīr, i.e. the camel grew weary and tired; and one says ḥasara al-baʿīr and ḥasartuhu (I wearied it), so it is both intransitive and transitive; and also aḥsartuhu, so faʿala and afʿala have one meaning. More explanation of al-istiḥsār will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا يا وَيْلَنا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ): يا is a vocative particle and ويلنا is the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), a muḍāf. They call upon woe and ruin, because this is its time. It is also possible that يا is for drawing attention and ويلنا is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb. The clause is the object of their speech (maqūl al-qawl). إنّ and its noun, and the clause كنا ظالمين is its khabar (predicate); [كنا is] kāna and its noun, and ظالمين is its khabar. (فَما زالَتْ تِلْكَ دَعْواهُمْ حَتَّى جَعَلْناهُمْ حَصِيداً خامِدِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما زالت is a defective past verb and the tāʾ is the sign of the feminine; تلك, a demonstrative, is its noun, in the position of nominative; دعواهم is its khabar, accusative (manṣūb) with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the mīm is a particle indicating the masculine plural. What is meant by the "cry" is those words, namely «يا وَيْلَنا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظالِمِينَ». حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; جعلناهم is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); حصيدا خامدين is the second mafʿūl bihi, because the two together are treated as one, since the meaning of جعلناهم حصيدا خامدين is "We made them combine likeness to harvested crops and extinction". An example of that is your saying جعلته حلوا حامضا ("I made it sweet-sour"), i.e. combining the two flavours [Translator's note: the source prints «للطعين», evidently for «للطعمين»], i.e. tart. You may also make خامدين an adjective (naʿt) of حصيدا. (وَما خَلَقْنَا السَّماءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما لاعِبِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; the clause is resumptive, brought to present the marvels and wonders contained in the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them, for admonition, and to be occasions for taking heed and an incentive to reflection and inference. ما is negative; خلقنا is a verb and its fāʿil; السماء is the mafʿūl bihi; الأرض is conjoined to السماء; ما is conjoined to السماء and الأرض; بينهما is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and لاعبين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of خلقنا. (لَوْ أَرَدْنا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ لَهْواً لَاتَّخَذْناهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا إِنْ كُنَّا فاعِلِينَ): لو is a conditional particle of non-occurrence; أردنا is a verb and its fāʿil; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), the object of أردنا; the fāʿil of نتخذ is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we"; لهوا is the mafʿūl bihi. لاتخذناه: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو, and اتخذناه is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; من لدنا is attached to an omitted second object of اتخذ. إن may be negative, meaning ما, and كنا فاعلين is kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of اتخذناه, i.e. "while We are not doers [of that]". It is also possible that إن is conditional, its apodosis omitted and indicated by the apodosis of لو; perhaps this is preferable and the closer of the two views to the way of Arabic. (بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْباطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذا هُوَ زاهِقٌ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ): بل is a turning away (iḍrāb) from taking amusement and play, and a declaration of His transcendence above it, exalted be He in Himself. نقذف is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "we"; بالحق, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to نقذف; على الباطل is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "rising above falsehood". فيدمغه is conjoined to نقذف. فإذا: the fāʾ is a conjunction and إذا is of surprise (fujāʾiyya), mentioned before; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and زاهق its khabar. ولكم: the wāw is resumptive; لكم is a fronted khabar and الويل a postponed mubtadaʾ; مما is attached to the "settledness" (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached, namely مما [Translator's note: so in the source; the khabar is لكم], i.e. "woe is settled for you from all that you describe". ما [in مما] may be relative or maṣdariyya, and in either case the clause تصفون has no grammatical position. (وَلَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the wāw is a conjunction; له is a fronted khabar and من a postponed mubtadaʾ; في السموات والأرض is the ṣila. (وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبادَتِهِ وَلا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; من is conjoined to the first من; عنده is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila; the clause لا يستكبرون is a ḥāl of the first من; عن عبادته is attached to يستكبرون; and the clause لا يستحسرون is conjoined to the clause لا يستكبرون. It is also possible that the wāw is resumptive and ومن عنده, i.e. the angels, is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause لا يستكبرون, the clause being resumptive. (يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ لا يَفْتُرُونَ): a resumptive clause, brought to affirm what those who are with Allah do in their worship. يسبحون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause may also be a ḥāl. الليل and النهار are two adverbs attached to يسبحون, and the clause لا يفترون is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يسبحون. (أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ هُمْ يُنْشِرُونَ): أم is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, a conjunction conveying denial; اتخذوا is a verb and its fāʿil; آلهة is the mafʿūl bihi, and من الأرض is an adjective; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause ينشرون is the khabar; the clause هم ينشرون is an adjective of آلهة. The object of ينشرون is omitted, i.e. "they bring the dead to life". It may also be made a resumptive clause. They did not claim for their gods that they raise the dead, but by merely claiming their divinity they are bound to claim implicitly that they raise the dead. More discussion of the pronoun «هم» will come in the section on rhetoric. (لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا فَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ): لو is a conditional particle of non-occurrence; كان is a defective past verb; فيهما is the fronted khabar of كان and آلهة its postponed noun; إلا, meaning غير ("other than"), is an adjective of آلهة whose case-ending appears on what follows it. It cannot be an exceptive particle, because the implication of the exception is corrupt here: its upshot would be that if there were in them gods from whom Allah was not excepted, they would not be ruined — and that is not so, for the mere multiplicity of gods necessarily entails ruin absolutely. A fuller exposition of this important discussion will come. لفسدتا: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو, and the clause فسدتا has no grammatical position. فسبحان الله: the fāʾ is a conjunction, ordering what follows it upon what precedes it, namely the establishment of oneness by demonstration; سبحان is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; رب العرش is a badal (substitute) or an adjective of the Name of Majesty; عما is attached to سبحان; and the clause يصفون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما; ما may also be maṣdariyya. (لا يُسْئَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْئَلُونَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to show that He, glory be to Him, is alone in sovereignty, such that no one asks Him about what He does. لا is negative; يسأل is an imperfect verb in the passive, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being "He"; عما is attached to يسأل. وهم: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يسألون is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are numerous devices, the first of which:
1- Metaphor (istiʿāra) in their saying «يا ويلنا»: they addressed woe, which is destruction, as though it were a living person whom they call upon to save them from what they are in.
2- The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh) in His saying «جَعَلْناهُمْ حَصِيداً خامِدِينَ».
After the punishment had befallen them, He likened them first to حصيد, which is harvested crops, the point of resemblance between the likened and that to which it is likened being uprooting from the places of growth. Then He likened them secondly to an extinguished fire of which nothing remains but dead embers, with no benefit in them and no capacity for any benefit from them; so you see nothing but scattered remains and dispersed parts, stretched out and overcome by decay [Translator's note: the source prints «وقدران», evidently for «وقد ران»].
3- Implied metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya) in His saying «بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق»: He likened truth and falsehood, which are abstract, to two material, perceptible things that are hurled and pushed; then He omitted these two things and borrowed what belongs to them, namely hurling and crushing (al-damgh), to embody the overthrow of falsehood and the truth's rising above it, and to depict its nullification, annulment and effacement, as though it were a hard body such as a rock or something like it in strength and hardness, hurled upon a soft, hollow body and crushing its brain. It is a metaphor of the perceptible for the intelligible. A detailed discussion of that, with a complete account of the kinds of metaphor in relation to the two terms of the simile, has preceded.
4- Strength of wording for strength of meaning: this device has been discussed before. We mean by it moving a word from one pattern to another, longer pattern, so that it contains more of the meaning it indicates than it contained at first; for words are indicators of meanings and models for expressing them, so when the words are increased, the division requires an increase in meanings. This kind of increase is used only in contexts of hyperbole, and here it is in the saying of the Exalted «وَلا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ». He turned from the triliteral, ḥasara, to the six-letter form, istaḥsara. The apparent form of the speech would have been to say يحسرون, i.e. "they grow weary and tired", since even the slightest boredom or weariness is inconceivable on the part of the angels with respect to their worship of Allah, glory be to Him. But He turned away from that for a secret hidden to a first, superficial glance: namely that their absorption in worship and their total devotion to it would call for the utmost and extreme degree of weariness.
5- Making the pronoun explicit: this is in His saying «هم ينشرون». It would have sufficed to say ينشرون, but He turned from that to making the pronoun explicit, first to convey the meaning of exclusivity, as though they had said "there is no one here able to raise the dead except them", and secondly to record their being bound to claim divine attributes for their gods. Allah nullified this claim in the verse following this one by the proof of mutual hindrance (dalīl al-tamānuʿ), drawn from the sea of this verse, namely «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا», as will be clarified in the i'rab [Translator's note: so in the source]. This is of the essence and pure substance of speech.
6- The dialectical method (al-madhhab al-kalāmī): this is in His saying «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا». Ibn al-Muʿtazz mentioned that the one who gave it this name was al-Jāḥiẓ, and the Noble Book is filled with it. Its definition is that the speaker argues for what he wants to establish with a proof that silences his opponent, in the manner of the theologians (arbāb al-kalām). It has numerous ways; al-Rummānī, in his commentary called al-Nukat fī Iʿjāz al-Qur'an, brought them to five kinds. Among them is casting the speech in the form of doubt, for the sake of utmost fairness. The entailment of His saying «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا» is that they have not been ruined, so there are no gods in them except Allah. The explanation of that is that the proof of mutual hindrance is that if another god existed alongside Allah [Translator's note: the sentence is incomplete in the source] — they might say: if we suppose the existence of two gods, then either both are described by the attributes of perfection, which include the power to give life to the dead and raise them and other possible things, or neither of them has them, or one of them has them and not the other; and then the subjects would be ruined by the management of the two kings, because of the mutual struggle for dominance, mutual rejection and disagreement that would arise between them. It is reported that ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān, when he killed ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Ashdaq, said: "By Allah, he was dearer to me than the blood of my eye, but two stallions do not come together in one herd of she-camels." The theologians have wide-ranging excursions on the method of mutual hindrance, which are to be found in their proper places, and its clarification will come in the section on benefits.

* Benefits:
«إلا» in the sense of «غير»:
The basic function of «إلا» is exception, and of «غير» description; then one may be treated like the other, so that إلا is used for description and غير for exception. If إلا is in the sense of غير, it and what follows it occur as an adjective of what precedes it. That is where exception is not intended by it, but rather the description of what precedes it as being other than what follows it, as in the saying of the Exalted «لَوْ كانَ فِيهِما آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتا». إلا and what follows it are an adjective of آلهة, because what is meant is the negation of multiple gods and the affirmation of the one, single God. The exception with the accusative is not valid, because the meaning would then be: "If there were in them gods among whom Allah was not, they would be ruined", which implies that if there were in them gods among whom Allah was, they would not be ruined — and this is evidently corrupt. May Allah forgive Ibn Yaʿīsh, the commentator on al-Zamakhsharī's al-Mufaṣṣal, for he permitted the accusative as an exception in the noble verse without appreciating the corruption that follows from the accusative. Ibn Yaʿīsh's wording is: "Allah the Exalted said: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا, and what is meant is 'other than Allah'; so this can only be a description. It cannot be a badal intended as exception, because it would then amount to 'if there were in them [none] but Allah, they would be ruined', and that is corrupt, because لو is a condition regarding the past, so it is like إن regarding the future; and if you said إن أتاني إلا زيد it would not be valid, because the condition is treated as affirmative, so just as أتاني إلا زيد is not valid, so إن أتاني إلا زيد is not valid. But if it were made accusative as an exception, and you said 'لو كان فيهما إلا الله', it would be permissible." [Translator's note: the quoted sentence appears thus in the source; the example given still lacks the excepted-from noun.] Further, the Name of Majesty cannot be parsed as a badal of آلهة either, because where exception is not valid, substitution is not valid. Moreover, the statement is affirmative, so substitution would not be permissible even if exception were valid, because the accusative is obligatory in a complete affirmative statement.
