Abū Tammām can be considered the master of a special way in the kalāmī method. Listen to his saying on envy:
وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة ... طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود
لولا اشتعال النار فيما جاورت ... ما كان يعرف طيب عرف العود
(When Allah wills to spread a virtue that has been folded away, He provides for it the tongue of an envier. / Were it not for the fire's blazing in what lies next to it, the sweetness of the scent of aloes-wood would not be known.)
And among the flowers of Bahāʾ al-Dīn Zuhayr is his saying:
يا من أكابد فيه ما أكابده ... مولاي أصبر حتى يحكم الله
سميت غيرك محبوبي مغالطة ... لمعشر فيك قد فاهوا بما فاهوا
أقول زيد وزيد لست أعرفه ... وإنما هو لفظ أنت معناه
وكم ذكرت مسمّى لا اكتراث به ... حتى يجر إلى ذكراك ذكراه
أتيه فيك على العشاق كلهم ... قد عز من أنت، يا مولاي، مولاه
كادت عيونهم بالبغض تنطق لي ... حتى كأن عيون الناس أفواه
(O you for whom I suffer what I suffer, my lord, I shall be patient until Allah decides. / I called someone other than you my beloved, to mislead a company who have blurted out what they blurted about you. / I say "Zayd, and Zayd", whom I do not know, but it is only a word of which you are the meaning. / How many a named one I have mentioned of no concern to me, until its mention drew on the mention of you. / I am proud over all lovers on your account; he is mighty whose master, my lord, you are. / Their eyes almost spoke to me with hatred, until the eyes of people seemed to be mouths.)

dervis-irab:101-105.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السِّجِلِّ): the book of covenants and the book of judgments; a book in which the judge writes down the form of claims and the ruling in them, and deeds of sale and the like, so that they remain preserved with him. Its plural is sijillāt. One says sajjala al-rajul: he wrote the sijill; sajjala al-awrāq: he registered the papers in the courts; sajjala al-qāḍī ʿalayhi: the judge pronounced judgment on him; sajjala ʿalayhi bi-kadhā: he made him notorious for it and branded him; and sajjala lahu bi-mālihi: he confirmed it and established it for him.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنى أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ) «إن» and its noun; the clause «سبقت» is the ṣila (relative clause); «ولهم» is attached to «سبقت»; «ومنّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «والحسنى» is the fāʿil (agent); «وأولئك» is the mubtadaʾ; «وعنها» is attached to «مبعدون»; «ومبعدون» is the khabar of «أولئك»; the clause «أولئك عنها مبعدون» is the khabar of «إن»; and the clause «إن» etc. is inceptive.
(لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها وَهُمْ فِي مَا اشْتَهَتْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ خالِدُونَ) The clause «لا يسمعون حسيسها» admits several analyses: it may be a badal (substitute) for «مبعدون» because it takes its place and dispenses with it; it may be a second khabar of «أولئك»; and it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun of «مبعدون». «لا» is negative; «ويسمعون حسيسها» is an imperfect verb, nominative, with its agent and direct object. The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; «وهم» is the mubtadaʾ; «وفيما» is attached to «خالدون»; the clause «اشتهت أنفسهم» is the ṣila; and «وخالدون» is their khabar.
(لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الْفَزَعُ الْأَكْبَرُ وَتَتَلَقَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ هذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ) The clause is circumstantial, or a badal for the preceding clause. «لا» is negative; «ويحزنهم»: verb and direct object; «والفزع» is the agent; «والأكبر» is an adjective of «الفزع»; «وتتلقاهم الملائكة»: verb, direct object and agent. The clause «هذا يومكم» is the content of an omitted saying occupying the position of a ḥāl, i.e. "saying: This is your day"; «وهذا» is the mubtadaʾ and «ويومكم» the khabar; «والذي» is an adjective of «يومكم»; the clause «كنتم» is the ṣila; kāna and its noun; and the clause «توعدون» is the khabar of «كنتم».
(يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّماءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ) The adverb is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember"; you may attach it to «لا يحزنهم», or to «الفزع», or to «تتلقاهم الملائكة». The clause «نطوي» is in the position of genitive, the adverb being annexed to it; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we (naḥnu)"; «والسماء» is the direct object; «وكطي»: the kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "as a man folds his page in order to write in it"; so al-ṭayy is a maṣdar annexed to its object, and omission of the agent with the maṣdar is regular and continual. «وللكتب» is attached to «طي», the lām serving to strengthen transitivity, i.e. "for the writings, all of them", that is, for the many things of meaning that are written in it.
(كَما بَدَأْنا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ وَعْداً عَلَيْنا إِنَّا كُنَّا فاعِلِينَ) The kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; «وما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); «وبدأنا»: verb and agent; «وأول خلق» is the direct object of «بدأنا», i.e. "We shall restore the first creation in a restoring like Our beginning of it"; al-Zamakhsharī always makes «ما» a restraining particle (kāffa) for the kāf. «ووعدا» is a maṣdar made accusative by an implied «وعدنا» before it, and is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) confirming the content of what precedes; «وعلينا» is attached to «وعدا»; «وإن» and its noun; the clause «كنا» is the khabar of «إنا»; kāna and its noun; «وفاعلين» is its khabar. The clause «إنا» is causal, serving as emphasis on the power to do that; Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr implied it as "that is, we are able to do that"; al-ʿImādī preferred that it be circumstantial and implied it as "that is, making this promise come true, so prepare for it". Important benefits on this verse will come in the sections on Benefits and Rhetoric. [Translator's note: this entry in the data contains no separate Benefits section; the author's cross-reference is translated as written.]
(وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنا فِي الزَّبُورِ مِنْ بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ أَنَّ الْأَرْضَ يَرِثُها عِبادِيَ الصَّالِحُونَ) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to establish that the earth belongs to the righteous, for them to exploit its resources and the energies stored within it. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «وقد» is a particle of affirmation; «وكتبنا»: verb and agent; «وفي الزبور» is attached to «كتبنا»; «ومن بعد» is attached to an omitted element serving as a ḥāl from «الزبور»; «وأن» and what is in its scope is the object of «كتبنا», i.e. "We wrote the inheritance of the earth"; «وإن» and its noun, and the clause «يرثها» its khabar; «وعبادي» is the agent and «والصالحون» an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- Exaggeration (mubālagha): in His saying «لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها» there is the art of exaggeration, because someone might say: "When the people of Paradise have settled in their abodes there, what glad tidings is there for them in that they do not hear its faintest sound?" The answer is that it is an emphatic exaggeration, and that it (Hell) will never come near them; for whoever is close to it hears, without doubt, its faintest sound, because the people of the Fire are in levels (darakāt) arranged in accordance with the number of its inhabitants and of those who enter it, and in accordance with the number of their objects of worship. For that reason the Exalted said in another verse «لَها سَبْعَةُ أَبْوابٍ لِكُلِّ بابٍ مِنْهُمْ جُزْءٌ مَقْسُومٌ», and the detail of that will come in Sūrat al-Ḥijr. It is related that ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, recited this verse, «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنى أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ», and then said: "I am one of them, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar and ʿUthmān and Ṭalḥa and al-Zubayr and Saʿd and Saʿīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf." Then the prayer was called and he stood up dragging his cloak, saying: «لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها».
2- Simile (tashbīh): in His saying «كَما بَدَأْنا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ» there is a likening of the restoration to the beginning, in that power reaches both equally. Al-Zamakhsharī said:
"If you say: What is the first creation that He should restore it as He began it? I say: Its first is bringing it into being from nothing, so as He brought it into being first from nothing, He restores it a second time from nothing. If you say: Why is «خلق» indefinite? I say: It is like your saying 'he is the first man who came to me', meaning the first of the men, but you made it singular and indefinite, wishing to itemise them man by man; so likewise the meaning of 'first creation' is the first of creation, in the sense of the first of created things, because khalq is a maṣdar that is not pluralised. There is another aspect, that the kāf is made accusative by an implied verb that «نعيده» explains, and «ما» is a relative: 'We restore the like of that which We began, We restore it'; and «أول خلق» is an adverbial expression attached to «بدأناه», i.e. 'the first of what He created', or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the relative, which has dropped out of the wording but is established in the meaning."

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ مُّحْدَثٍ﴾: had al-muḥdath been accusative or nominative, it would have been correct. The accusative would be by the verb: "there does not come to them, newly revealed…"; the nominative would be by referring back to the underlying sense of al-dhikr, because if you dropped (مِن) you would put al-dhikr in the nominative. It is like your saying: "mā min aḥadin qāʾimin", "qāʾimun" and "qāʾiman" ("there is no one standing"). The accusative in this [Translator's note: last example] rests on the acceptability of the bāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. as with mā… bi-qāʾimin, as transmitted], and in the first on the verb.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ is accusative by conjunction with His saying ﴿وهم يلعبونَ﴾, because His saying "while they play" is on a par with "playing" (lāʿibīna); so it is as if: "except that they listen to it playing, their hearts distracted." Its accusative may also be by deriving it from the pronoun implied in (يلعبُون): they play thus, their hearts distracted. Had you put (لاهية) in the nominative, making it follow yalʿabūna, it would have been correct, as you say: "ʿAbd Allāh is amusing himself (yalhū) and playing (lāʿibun)." Similar to it is the poet's saying:
* يَقْصِدُ فى أَسْوُقها وجائر *
(He aims straight at their shanks, and he is erring.)
It may also be nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), not by referring back to yalʿabūna.
His saying ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجْوَى﴾: it was said wa-asarrū only because it refers to "the people" (al-nās), who were described with amusement and play; and (الذينَ) follows al-nās and is genitive, as though you had said: "Drawn near for the people whose state is this." If you wish, you make (الذين) a new beginning, nominative, as though you made it an explanation of the nouns [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun] in asarrū, as He said ﴿فَعَمُوا وصَمُّوا ثمَّ تَابَ اللهُ عليهم ثم عَمُوا وصَمُّوا كثير منهم.﴾

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّي﴾ and ﴿قُل ربّى﴾: all is correct.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلاَمٍ بَلِ ٱفْتَرَاهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ﴾: it is turned with bal on the sense of their denial, even though the speech expressing their denial has not appeared before it, because its meaning is an address to, and a report about, the deniers.
His saying: ﴿فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِآيَةٍ كَمَآ أُرْسِلَ ٱلأَوَّلُونَ﴾: like the signs which the former ones brought.

farraa:6-6.t: So Allah said ﴿مَآ آمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَآ﴾, of those to whom a sign came; so how should these believe?

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿فَاسْئَلُوۤاْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾: that is, the people of the books, the Torah and the Gospel.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ جَسَداً لاَّ يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ﴾: He made jasad singular and did not pluralize it — and that is good Arabic — because jasad is like your saying "an embodied thing", since it is derived from a verb, so it suffices for the plural; likewise the reading of whoever read ﴿لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سَقْفاً من فِضَّةٍ﴾, the meaning being "roofs". Then He said ﴿لا يأكلونَ الطعَام﴾: He is saying: We made them bodies only so that they would eat food, ﴿وَمَا كانوا خالدينَ﴾ by their eating and drinking — meaning the men who were sent [116 a]. Had it been said "lā yaʾkulu al-ṭaʿām" (singular), it would have been correct, making the verb belong to al-jasad, just as you say: "You two are two righteous things", and "a righteous thing", and "a thing, two righteous ones" [Translator's note: so in the text]. Similar to it is ﴿أَمَنةً نُعَاساً تَغْشَى طائِفَةً﴾ and ﴿يَغْشَى﴾; and similar to it is ﴿إنَّ شَجَرةَ الزقُّومِ طَعَامُ الأثيمِ﴾ — He said ﴿كَالمُهْلِ تَغْلِى﴾ with reference to the tree, and (يَغْلِى) with reference to the food; and likewise His saying ﴿أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنْىّ يُمْنَى﴾ and tumnā.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿كِتَاباً فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ﴾: your honour.

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿إِذَا هُمْ مِّنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ﴾: they flee and are routed.

farraa:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿فَمَا زَالَت تِلْكَ دَعْوَاهُمْ﴾ means their saying "We have indeed been wrongdoers", i.e. they kept on repeating it. In this place the masculine would also be suitable; it is like His saying ﴿ذَلَكَ مِنْ أنْباءِ الغَيْبِ﴾ and ﴿تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الغَيْبِ﴾.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْ أَرَدْنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ لَهْواً﴾: al-Farrāʾ said: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-lahw is "child" in the dialect of Ḥaḍramawt.
His saying: ﴿إِن كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ﴾: it has come in the exegesis: "We were not doers [Translator's note: of that]." (إنْ) may have the meaning of (ما), as in His saying ﴿إنْ أَنْتَ إلاّ نَذِيرٌ﴾. And it may be the in that has the role of a condition (jazāʾ), so it would be: "if We were doers — and We do not do it." That is the closer of the two ways to the approach of Arabic, and Allah knows best.

farraa:22-22.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ آلِهَةٌ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا﴾: illā in this place is on a par with siwā ("other than"), as though you said: "Were there gods in them other than (or besides) Allah, their inhabitants would have been ruined" (meaning the inhabitants of heaven and earth).

farraa:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ عِبَادٌ مُّكْرَمُونَ﴾: its meaning is "rather, they are honoured servants". Had it been "bal ʿibādan mukramīna" (accusative), referred back to al-walad, i.e. "We did not take them as a child, but We took them as honoured servants", (it would have been correct).

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقاً فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا﴾: the sky was split open with rain and the earth with vegetation. (He said) (كَانَتَا رَتْقاً) and did not say ratqayn (dual); (it is) as He said ﴿مهما جَعَلناهم جَسَداً﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse (21:8) reads «وما جعلناهم جسدا»].
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ is genitive. Had it been ḥayyan (accusative), it would have been correct, i.e. "We made everything living from water."

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ سَقْفاً مَّحْفُوظاً﴾: had it been said maḥfūẓatan, the feminine would refer to al-samāʾ and the masculine to al-saqf, as He said ﴿أَمَنَةً نُعَاساً تَغْشَى﴾ and (يَغْشَى). And it was called (a roof) though it is heavens because it is a roof over the earth like the roof over a house. The meaning of His saying (مَّحْفُوظاً): it is guarded (from the devils) by the stars.
His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾: its signs are its moon, its sun and its stars. Mujāhid read (وهم عن آياتِها مُعْرِضونَ) [Translator's note: the source prints the plural here; the following words indicate that Mujāhid's reading was the singular «آيتها»], making it singular (and making) the sky with what is in it a single sign. All is correct.

farraa:33-33.t: And He said: ﴿فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ for non-humans — for the sun, the moon, the night and the day. That is because swimming is among the acts of humans, so it was said with the nūn [Translator's note: of the masculine rational plural], just as it was said ﴿والشمسَ والقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِى سَاجِدِين﴾, because prostration is among the acts of humans. It is said that al-falak is a restrained wave in which they run.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلْخَالِدُونَ﴾: the fāʾ has entered the condition — which is (إن) — and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because the condition is connected to Qurʾān before it; so the alif of interrogation was placed in it before the fāʾ of the condition. The fāʾ entered His saying (فهم) because it is the apodosis of the condition. Had the fāʾ been dropped from His saying (فهم), it would have been correct for two reasons. One of them is that you intend the fāʾ and imply it, because it does not change (هم) from its nominative; in such a place implication is suitable. The other reason is that (هم) is meant to be brought forward to the fāʾ, so it is as though [116 b] it were said: "Will they be the immortals if you die?"

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ﴾: had you given tanwīn to (ذائقة) and put (الموت) in the accusative, it would have been correct. What the Arabs mostly choose is tanwīn and the accusative for the future; when its meaning is past, they hardly say it other than with the construct (iḍāfa). As for the future, it is your saying "anā ṣāʾimun yawma al-khamīs" ("I am fasting on Thursday") when it is a coming Thursday; if you report the fast of a past Thursday, you say "anā ṣāʾimu yawmi al-khamīs". This is the way of governing (al-ʿamal). They also choose tanwīn when it comes with negation; of that is their saying "mā huwa bi-tārikin ḥaqqahu" and "huwa ghayru tārikin ḥaqqahu" ("he is not one to give up his right"); they hardly ever omit the tanwīn [Translator's note: there]. Yet omitting it is common and permissible, and they recite the saying of Abū al-Aswad:
فألفَيْتُه غير مستعتب * ولا ذاكرِ اللهَ إلا قليلاَ
(I found him not seeking to make amends, nor remembering Allah except a little.)
Whoever drops the nūn and uses the accusative says: the intention is tanwīn with negation, but I dropped the nūn because of the quiescent letter it met, while giving it its governing force. Whoever uses the genitive has made it a construct (iḍāfa).

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿أَهَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾: He means: who disparages your gods. Likewise His saying ﴿سَمِعْنَا فَتَى يَذْكُرُهم يُقَالُ لَهُ إبراهِيمُ﴾, i.e. disparages them. You say to a man: "If you mention me, you will surely regret it", while you mean: with ill. ʿAntara said:
لا تذكرى مُهْرِى وَمَا أطعمتُهُ * فيكونَ جِلْدكِ مثل جِلد الأشهبِ
(Do not mention my colt and what I have fed him, lest your skin become like the skin of the grey horse.)
That is, do not reproach me for preferring my colt; so he made dhikr mean reproach.

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿خُلِقَ ٱلإنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾, and "ʿalā ʿajal": it is as though you said: "I built him and created him out of haste and upon haste."

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَـٰذَا ٱلْوَعْدُ إِن كُنتُمْ﴾: (مَتَي) is in the position of the accusative, because if you made its answer overt you would see it in the accusative and say: "The promise is on such-and-such a day (yawma)." (And if) you made (متى) be in the position of the nominative, as you say "When is the appointment?" and he says "yawmu al-khamīs" or "yawma al-khamīs" [Translator's note: both are possible]. Allah said ﴿مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ﴾; had you used the accusative, it would have been correct. When you make the appointment an indefinite of days, nights, months and years, you use the nominative and say [Translator's note: the text has «فلقت», evidently for «فقلت»]: "Your appointment is a day or two days, a night or two nights", as Allah said ﴿غُدُوُّهَا شَهْرٌ وَرَوَاحُهَا شَهْرٌ﴾. The Arabs say: "The cold is only two months" and "the summer is only two months"; had it come in the accusative, it would have been correct. They chose the nominative only because you have left the two months unspecified, so the two together became as it were a time-span for the summer. They chose the accusative with the definite only because it is a known time, assigned to what follows it, so the adverbial (al-ṣifa) is good — just as you say "ʿAbd Allāh is a dūnun among men" (nominative, "inferior"), and "ʿAbd Allāh is dūnaka" (below you), using the accusative. Similar to it: "The two armies met; the Muslims were a side (jānibun) and the unbelievers a side." When you add a genitive you use the accusative and say: "The Muslims were on the side of (jāniba) their companion, and the unbelievers on the side of their companion." When you do not put jānib in construct, you make them themselves like the side, not that they are in it. Make analogies on this basis.

farraa:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ﴾, and His saying: ﴿فَمَنْ يَنْصُرُنِى مِنَ الله إن عَصَيْتُه﴾: "who will protect me?" That is its meaning — and Allah knows best — throughout the Qurʾān.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ مَن يَكْلَؤُكُم﴾
is hamzated. (If) you dropped [117 a] the hamza of something like it outside the Qurʾān, you would say yaklūkum with a quiescent wāw, or yaklākum with a quiescent alif, like yakhshākum. Whoever makes it a quiescent wāw says kalān [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps «كَلاَت» is meant] with alif, dropping the glottal stop (al-nabra) from it; and whoever says yaklākum says kalaytu, like qaḍaytu; that is of the dialect of Quraysh. All is good, except that in both ways they say maklūwa without hamza, and maklūw without hamza is more frequent than their saying makliyya. Had makliyy been said in the dialect of those who say kalaytu, it would have been correct. I heard one of the Arabs recite the saying of al-Farazdaq:
وما خاصم الاقوامَ مِن ذى خُصُومةٍ * كَورْهاء مَشْنِىّ إليها حَليلُها
(No disputant ever disputed with people like a foolish woman whose husband is hated by her.)
So he built it on shanītu, dropping the glottal stop. His saying ﴿مَن يَكْلَؤُكُم بِٱلْلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ﴾: He means "from the command of the Most Merciful"; "command" has been omitted while it is meant, as He said in another place ﴿فَمَنْ يَنْصُرنِى مِنَ اللهِ﴾, meaning: who will protect me from the punishment of Allah? And He made the meaning overt in another place, saying ﴿فَمَنْ يَنْصُرُنَا مِنْ بَأْسِ اللهِ إِنْ جَاءنَا﴾.

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ means the gods: they cannot protect themselves. ﴿وَلاَ هُمْ مِّنَّا يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ means the unbelievers, i.e. they are not given protection (and they [Translator's note: the gods] are not protected from Us). Do you not see that the Arabs say "(He was a protector (jār) to us)", meaning: he grants you protection and defends you? So He said (يُصْحَبُونَ) in the sense of granting protection [Translator's note: the text has «بالإجازة»; «بالإجارة», "protection", is evidently meant].

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَسْمَعُ ٱلصُّمُّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ﴾: you put (الصُمّ) in the nominative because the act is theirs. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (وَلاَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعَاءَ), putting (الصم) in the accusative because the act falls upon it.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَازِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ﴾: al-qisṭ is a description of the scales even though it is singular; it is on a par with your saying to a group: "You are contentment and justice." Likewise al-ḥaqq: when it describes one, two or more, it remains singular.
His saying: ﴿لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾: and "on the Day of Resurrection".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَتَيْنَا بِهَا﴾: it refers to al-ḥabba ("the grain"); had it been atainā bihi, (it would have been correct) because mithqāl is masculine. Had al-mithqāl been put in the nominative, as He said ﴿وإنْ كَانَ ذُو عُسْرَة فَنِظرةٌ﴾, it would have been correct. Mujāhid read (آتَيْنَا بهَا) with a long alif, meaning: "We requited for it", on the pattern fāʿalnā; that is a good option.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ وَضِيَآءً﴾: it is a description of al-furqān, and its meaning — and Allah knows best — is "We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion as a light and a reminder"; the wāw entered as He said ﴿إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ الكوَاكِب وَحِفْظاً﴾, i.e. "We made that"; and likewise (and a light and a reminder): "We gave that."

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿وَهَـٰذَا ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ﴾: al-mubārak is nominative as a description of al-dhikr. Had it been accusative, as in your saying "We sent it down blessed", it would have been correct.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ رُشْدَهُ﴾: his guidance, when he was in the underground hiding-place, until Allah brought him to what He brought him. Similar to it is ﴿وَلَوْ شئنا لآتَيْنَا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ هُدَاهَا﴾: its right guidance.

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿وَتَٱللَّهِ لأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَامَكُمْ بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّواْ مُدْبِرِينَ﴾: they had wanted to go out to a festival of theirs, and Abraham excused himself from them and stayed behind (and said): "I am ill." When they had gone, he smashed their gods except the biggest of them. When they returned, one of them said: "I heard Abraham say: By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols." That is His saying ﴿سَمِعْنَا فَتيً يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَال لَهُ إبراهيم﴾: he mentions them with disparagement (and abuse), and with what he said about plotting.

farraa:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُمْ جُذَاذاً﴾: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it (جِذَاذاً), and the reading of the people otherwise [117 b] is (جُذَاذاً) with ḍamma. Whoever says (جُذَاذاً), giving the jīm ḍamma, it is a singular, like al-ḥuṭām and al-rufāt ("debris", "crumbled remains"). Whoever says (جِذَاذاً) with kasra, it is a plural, as though it were jadhīdh and jidhādh, like khafīf and khifāf.

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ أَعْيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾: in front of everyone. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ against him with what the one person testified to. And it is said: perhaps they will witness his affair and what is done to him.

farraa:63-63.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَـٰذَا﴾: some people said "bal faʿallahu kabīruhum", with the doubled consonant, meaning "fa-laʿallahu kabīruhum" ("perhaps it was their biggest one"). Some people said: "Rather, their biggest one did it, if they can speak", making the act of the biggest one dependent on "if they can speak", while they cannot speak. The approach that the generality follow is "بَلْ فَعَلَهُ", just as Joseph said ﴿أَيَّتُها العِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ لَسَارِقُونَ﴾, while they had not stolen. Allah has supported His prophets with more than this.

farraa:65-65.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ نُكِسُواْ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمْ﴾: He is saying: they turned back when they recognized Abraham's argument, and said: ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ يَنطِقُونَ﴾. (Knowing and thinking are on a par with an oath; for that reason ʿalima is met with mā) — so He said: ﴿عَلِمْتَ مَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾, like one's saying: "By Allah, you are not our brother"; and likewise His saying: ﴿وظَنُّوا مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ﴾.
Had the Arabs put (أنْ) before (ما), so that it was said "ʿalimtu an mā fīka khayr" and "ẓanantu an mā fīka khayr", it would have been correct. But when one of these verbs meets a particle such as (إن) accompanied by the lām, or an interrogative — as in your saying "Find out for me: did ʿAbd Allāh stand or Zayd?" — (or la-in) or law, they make do with that particle and do not put (أَنْ) before it. Do you not see His saying ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُم مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ﴾? Had it been said "an la-yasjununnahu", it would have been correct, as the poet said:
وخبَّرتما أن إنمَّا بين بيشَةٍ * ونَجْرانَ أَحوى والمحلُّ خَصيب
(And you two told me that between Bīsha and Najrān it is dark green with pasture, and the camping-ground is fertile.)
He put an before innamā; for that reason we have allowed its entry before the rest of the particles I have described to you.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿ وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً﴾: al-nāfila ("the extra gift") refers to Jacob specifically, because he is a grandson; that is how it has reached me.

farraa:74-74.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلُوطاً آتَيْنَاهُ﴾: Lūṭ is accusative by the hāʾ in ﴿آتَيْنَاه﴾ that refers back to him. The other accusative is by implying ﴿واذكر لوطا﴾ ("and mention Lot") or ﴿ولقد أرسلنا﴾ ("and We sent"), or whatever is mentioned at the beginning of the sūra; and even if it is not mentioned, the implied element is only from [Translator's note: the notion of] the sending or of the mentioning. Similar to it is ﴿وَلِسُلَيْمانَ الرِّيحَ﴾: (الريح) is accusative by an implied verb whose meaning is known: either "We subjected" or "We gave him".
Likewise His saying: ﴿ونُوحاً إذ نَادَى﴾ is by the implied [Translator's note: verb of] mentioning.
His saying: ﴿وَدَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمان﴾ — and all [Translator's note: the text has «وجمع», evidently for «وجميع»] the mentions of the prophets that come to you in this sūra — you put them in the accusative by coordination (nasaq) with what is accusative by the implied [Translator's note: verb of] mentioning.

farraa:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ﴾: al-nafsh is [Translator's note: grazing] by night. They were sheep belonging to a people that got into the vineyard of others. They brought their case to David, and he judged that the owners of the vineyard should have the sheep, and the vineyard be handed to the owners of the sheep. That reached his son Solomon, who said: "Something other than this would have been kinder to both parties." So David [Translator's note: the text has «دواد» for «داود»] adjured him to give judgement. He said: "I think the sheep should be handed to the owners of the vineyard, who will benefit from their milk, their young and their wool, and the vineyard handed to the owners of the sheep [118 a], who will tend it until it returns to its state on the day it was spoiled." It is related that the two values in this judgement [Translator's note: the text has «الحم», evidently for «الحكم»] were equal: the value of what they obtained from the sheep and the value of what the sheep had spoiled of the vineyard. That is His saying: ﴿فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا سُلَيْمَانَ﴾. And His saying: ﴿وَكُنَّا لحكمِهم﴾.
In one reading: (وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمَهِمَا شاهِدِين), and it is like His saying: ﴿فَإنْ كَانَ لَهُ إخْوَةٌ﴾, meaning two brothers or more. This is like His saying: ﴿لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَاهِدِينَ﴾, since He used the plural for two.

farraa:80-80.t: His saying: ﴿وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَّكُمْ لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ﴾, and (ليُحْصِنَكم) and (لنُحْصِنكم): whoever says (ليُحصنكم) with yāʾ does so because labūs is masculine; whoever says (لِتُحْصنكم) with tāʾ takes it to refer to ṣanʿa, which is feminine — or, if you wish, you make it feminine because of the coats of mail (al-durūʿ), since they are the labūs. Whoever reads (لنُحصنكم) with nūn is saying: "so that We may protect you". In this sense (ليُحصنكم) with yāʾ is also permissible: "so that Allah may protect you from your violence".

farraa:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: it used to run with Solomon to every place, then return with him the same day to his dwelling. That is His saying ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.

farraa:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلاً دُونَ ذٰلِكَ﴾: apart from the diving; He means other than diving: building.
His saying: ﴿وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَافِظِينَ﴾: for the devils. That is because they were kept from spoiling what they made. When one of the devils had finished his work, Solomon would assign him to another work, because when he finished what he was making and had no occupation, he would turn to demolishing what he had built. That is His saying: ﴿وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَافِظِينَ﴾.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَّعَهُمْ﴾: it is related that Job had seven sons and seven daughters, and they died during his affliction. When Allah removed it from him, Allah brought his sons and daughters back to life for him, and the like of them was born to him after that. That is His saying ﴿أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَّعَهُمْ رَحْمَةً﴾: We did that as a mercy.

farraa:87-87.t:
His saying: ﴿فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ﴾: He means that We would not decree for him the punishment that We decreed.
His saying: ﴿فَنَادَىٰ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ أَن لاَّ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ أَنتَ﴾: it is said: the darkness of the sea, and of the belly of the whale and its bowels (miʿā, with the short final vowel) in which Jonah was; those are the darknesses.

farraa:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نُنجِـي ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: the readers read it with two nūns, while its written form has one nūn. That is because the first nūn is vowelled and the second quiescent, and the quiescent one does not show in pronunciation; since it was hidden, it was dropped [Translator's note: in writing].
ʿĀṣim — as far as I know — read (نُجِّى) with one nūn and put (المؤمنين) in the accusative, as though he tolerated a grammatical error (laḥn); we know no explanation for it other than this: that a verb whose agent is not named, when it has a noun to itself, puts it in the nominative — unless the maṣdar (verbal noun) is implied in nujjiya, intended as the nominative, and (المؤمنين) put in the accusative. Then it would be like your saying "ḍuriba al-ḍarbu Zaydan" ("the beating was beaten Zayd"); then you refer to the beating by a pronoun and say "ḍuriba Zaydan". Likewise "nujjiya al-najāʾu al-muʾminīna".

farraa:90-90.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ﴾: He is saying: she was barren, and We made her bear children; that was her being set right.

farraa:91-91.t:
His saying: ﴿أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا﴾: the exegetes mentioned that it is the opening of her garment, and through it [Translator's note: the spirit] was breathed into her.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا وَٱبْنَهَآ آيَةً﴾ — (and He did not say "two signs") — because their affair is one. Had "two signs" been said, it would have been correct, because she gave birth while a virgin and Jesus spoke in the cradle; so they would be two signs, since they differ.

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ أُمَّتُكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾: you put (أمّة واحدة) in the accusative by "cutting off" (al-qaṭʿ) [Translator's note: the Kufan term for the ḥāl]. Al-Ḥasan put it in the nominative, (أمتكم أمةٌ واحدةٌ), making al-umma a khabar (predicate), then going back to "one community" with the nominative, also intending it as a khabar, like His saying: ﴿كَلاَّ إنَّهَا لَظَى نَزَّاعَةٌ لِلشَّوَى﴾.
In the reading of Ubayy, as far as I know: (إنَّها لإَحْدَى الكُبَر نَذِيرٌ للبَشَرِ}, the nominative by repetition (takrīr); and similar to it: (ذُو العَرْشِ المَجِيدُ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ).

farraa:95-95.t: His saying: ﴿وَحَرَامٌ عَلَىٰ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَآ﴾: Ibn ʿAbbās read it [Translator's note: the reading attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās appears to have dropped out of the text here; elsewhere it is reported as «وحِرْمٌ»]. More than one person narrated that to me, among them Hushaym from Dāwūd from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, and Sufyān from ʿUmayr and from Ibn ʿAbbās. ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated to me from his father from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: (وَحِرْمٌ). One of them narrated to me from Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī: (وحِرْمٌ عَلَى). The people of Medina and al-Ḥasan [Translator's note: read] (وحَرامٌ) with alif. Ḥarām is more widespread in recitation. It is on a par with your saying ḥill and ḥalāl, ḥirm and ḥarām.

farraa:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُمْ مِّن كُلِّ حَدَبٍ يَنسِلُونَ﴾: al-ḥadab is every hillock (and raised place).

farraa:97-97.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱقْتَرَبَ ٱلْوَعْدُ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "until, when it is opened, [Translator's note: the true promise] draws near." The entry of the wāw into the apodosis after (حَتّى إذا) is on a par with His saying ﴿حَتَّي إذا جَاءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ أَبوابُها﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (فَلَمَّا جَهَّزَهُمْ بِجَهَازِهم جَعَل السَّقَايَةَ) [Translator's note: the source quotes it without the wāw; the point is that ʿAbd Allāh's reading has «وجعل»], while in our reading it is without wāw. Similar to it in al-Ṣāffāt: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَسْلَمَا وَتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبينِ وَنَادَيْنَاهُ﴾, its meaning being "We called him". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فلمَّا أَجَزْنا سَاحَةَ الحىّ وانتحى * بنَا بَطْنُ خَبْتٍ ذِى قِفَاف عَقْنَقِل
(When we had crossed the open ground of the tribe, and the hollow of a plain with hillocks and winding sand-dunes drew us aside…)
He means "intaḥā" (without the wāw).
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا هِيَ شَاخِصَةٌ أَبْصَارُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾: (هى) may be a prop (ʿimād) [Translator's note: the Kufan term for the pronoun of the matter], in whose place (هو) would also be suitable; it would then be like His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ أَنَا اللهُ العَزِيزُ الحكِيمُ﴾. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿فَإنَّها لاَ تَعْمَى الأَبْصَارُ﴾: the feminine came because al-abṣār is feminine, while the masculine would be for the ʿimād. I heard one of the Arabs say: "kāna marratan wa-huwa yanfaʿu al-nāsa aḥsābuhum" ("once upon a time it was the case that people's noble lineages benefited them"), making (هو) an ʿimād. And one of them recited to me:
بثوب ودينارٍ وشاة ودرهمٍ * فَهَل هُوَ مرفوع بما هَا هنا راسُ
(With a garment, a dinar, a ewe and a dirham — is it the case that a head is raised by what is here?)
If you wish, you make (هى) refer to al-abṣār: you referred to them by a pronoun, then made al-abṣār overt to explain it, as the poet said:
لعمرُ أبيها لا تقول ظَعينتى * ألاَ فَرّعنى مالكُ بن أبى كعب
(By the life of her father, my lady in the litter will not say: "Ah, Mālik ibn Abī Kaʿb has abandoned me to fear!")
He mentioned al-ẓaʿīna when he had already referred to her by a pronoun in (laʿamru).

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾: it is related that al-ḥaṣab in the dialect of the people of Yemen is firewood (al-ḥaṭab). Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥakam al-Kāhilī from a man who heard ʿAlī read (حَطَب) with ṭāʾ. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā al-Madanī narrated to me from Abū al-Ḥuwayrith, tracing it back to ʿĀʾisha, that she read (حَطَبُ) likewise. And with a chain of Ibn Abī Yaḥyā from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read (حَضَب) with ḍād. Everything with which you stir up a fire or kindle it is ḥaḍab. As for al-ḥaṣab, it is, in the sense of the dialect of Najd, what you throw into the fire, as in your saying "ḥaṣabtu the man", i.e. I pelted him.

farraa:104-104.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ نَطْوِي ٱلسَّمَآءَ﴾: with nūn, and with tāʾ (تُطْوَى). Had it been said (يَطْوِى), as it was said (نطوى) with nūn, it would have been permissible.
The readers agreed on (السّجِلّ) with the doubled consonant.
Most of them say (للكِتَابِ), and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh (للكُتُب). Al-sijill is the scroll. The speech breaks off at "the books"; then it begins anew and says ﴿كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُّعِيدُهُ﴾: the kāf belongs to the creation, as though you said: "We will bring back the creation as We began them (the first time)."
His saying ﴿وَعْداً عَلَيْنَآ﴾ is like your saying "a duty upon Us" (ḥaqqan ʿalaynā).

farraa:105-105.t: His saying: ﴿أَنَّ ٱلأَرْضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِيَ ٱلصَّالِحُونَ﴾: it is said: the land of Paradise. And it is said: it is the land that the Children of Israel were promised, like His saying: ﴿وَأَوْرَثْنَا القَوْمَ الذِينَ كَانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفونَ مشَارِقَ الأرْضَ وَمغارِبَها﴾.

farraa:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ فِي هَـٰذَا لَبَلاَغاً﴾: that is, in the Qurʾān.

farraa:108-108.t:
His saying: ﴿يُوحَىٰ إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمْ﴾: the normal way of the speech is (anna with fatḥa), because (يُوحَى) falls upon it; and (إنَّما) with kasra is permissible. That is because it is a particle, as I described to you from the poet's saying:
* ... أَنْ إنَّما بَيْنَ بِيشَةٍ *
(…that between Bīsha…)
So you drop (أنْ), as though it were said: "It is only revealed to me that indeed your god is one god."

farraa:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿إِنْ أَدْرِي﴾ is nominative [Translator's note: i.e. indicative], in the sense of "I do not know".

farraa:112-112.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ ٱحْكُم بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ is jussive [Translator's note: i.e. imperative]: a request he made of his Lord. It has also been said: (قل رَبّى أحْكَمُ بالحق), with (أحكم) in the nominative and its alif given a hamza. Whoever says "qul rabbī aḥkamu bi-l-ḥaqq", the position of rabbī is nominative; and whoever says "rabbi -ḥkum" with the joining alif, it is in the position of the accusative as a vocative.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «في غَفْلَةٍ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) khabar (predicate); «مُعْرِضُونَ» is a second khabar, and the clause «وَهُمْ في غَفْلَةٍ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «النَّاسِ».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «ما يأتِيهِم من ذِكْرٍ» is resumptive; «ذِكْرٍ» is the fāʿil (agent) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The preposition and its genitive noun «من ربِّهِم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ذِكرِ»; «مُحْدَثٍ» is a naʿt of «ذكر»; the clause «اسْتَمَعُوهُ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «يأتيهم»; the clause «وَهُمْ يلْعَبُونَ» is a ḥāl of the agent of «استمعوه».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «لاهِيَةً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يلعبون», and «قُلوبُهم» is a fāʿil governed by «لاهية». «الذين» is a badal (substitute) of the wāw in «أَسَرُّوا». «بَشَرٌ» is the khabar (predicate) of «هذا», and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); «مِثْلُكُمْ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «بَشَر», and it did not acquire definiteness from the annexation because it is utterly vague. The clause «هل هذا إلا بَشَرٌ» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) of an omitted verb of saying which is a ḥāl of the wāw, i.e.: قائلين (saying). The clause «وأنتم تُبْصِرُونَ» is a ḥāl of the wāw in «تَأْتُونَ», and the clause «أَفَتَأْتُونَ» is conjoined to the object of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «في السَّماءِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «القول»; the clause «وهو السَّمِيعُ» is conjoined to the clause «رَبِّي يعلمُ», and «العَليمُ» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «بل» is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); «أَضْغَاثُ» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The fāʾ in His saying «فَلْيَأْتِنَا» links to the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: إن كان صادقًا فليأتنا (if he is truthful, let him bring us); the lām is the lām of command, and «يأتِنا» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter. The kāf is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e.: let him bring us a bringing like the sending of the former ones. The clause «أُرْسِلَ» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «قَرْيَةٍ» is the fāʿil (agent), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «أَهْلَكْنَاهَا» is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause «أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «آمَنَتْ».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «رِجَالا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the clause «نُوحِي» is a naʿt (adjective); the clause «فَاسْأَلُوا» is resumptive; the clause «إنْ كُنْتُم» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «جَسَدًا» is the second object; the clause «لا يَأْكُلُونَ» is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause «وما كانوا» is conjoined to the clause «ما جعلناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «الوَعْدَ» is the second object; «مَنْ» is a relative noun conjoined to the hāʾ in «أنجيناهم», and the clause «وَأَهْلَكْنَا» is conjoined to the clause «أنجيناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «لَقَدْ أَنزلْنَا» is the answer to the oath, and the implied (muqaddar) oath clause is resumptive. The clause «فيه ذِكْرُكُمْ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «كتابًا», and the clause «تعقلون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «كَمْ» is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كَمْ»; the clause «كانت» is a naʿt of «قَرْيَةٍ»; «آخَرِينَ» is a naʿt of «قَوْمًا».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوا» is conjoined to the clause {قَصَمْنَا}; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is the clause «إذا هُمْ مِنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ», and «إذا» is the «إذا» of surprise (fujāʾiyya); the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «لا تَرْكُضُوا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) of an implied (muqaddar) verb of saying. «ما» is a nominal relative in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ارْجِعُوا», and «مَسَاكِنِكُم» is a noun conjoined to «ما». The clause «لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْألُونَ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «يَا وَيْلَنَا»: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative, and its clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb); the clause «إنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِين» is the response to the vocative, resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «دَعْوَاهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما زال». «حتى» is a particle of limit and a preposition, and the maṣdar «أن جعلناهم» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (دَعْوَاهُم). «حصيدا» is the second object, and «وخامِدِين» belongs to the category of multiple objects, because the two objects are originally a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar. «حَصِيدًا» means "reaped" (maḥṣūdīn), the implied form being: like a reaped crop; that is why it was not made plural.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The adverb «بَيْنَهُمَا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); «لاعِبِينَ»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun «نا» in «خَلَقْنَا».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: (لو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «لَدُنْ» is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «اتخذناه». The clause «إن كُنَّا فَاعِلِين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «بَلْ نَقْذِفُ» is resumptive. The clause «فَيَدْمَغُهُ» is conjoined to the clause «نَقْذِفُ»; the fāʾ in «فإذا» is a conjunction and «إذا» is the «إذا» of surprise (fujāʾiyya); the clause «فإذا هو زَاهِقٌ» is conjoined to the clause «يَدْمَغُهُ». The clause «وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ» is resumptive. His saying «مما» is composed of the preposition «مِنْ» and the maṣdariyya «مَا», and the maṣdar is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the "being established" (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «وَلَهُ مَنْ» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and «مَنْ» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun «في السَّماوَات» is attached to the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause). The clause «وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ لا يستكبرون» is conjoined to the resumptive one, «ولَهُ منْ في السَّماوات»; the relative noun «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ, the adverb «عنده» is attached to the ṣila, and the clause «لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «مَنْ».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «يُسَبِّحُونَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ», and the clause «لا يَفْتُرُونَ» is a ḥāl of the agent of «يُسَبِّحُون».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «أَمْ» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) am, meaning bal plus the hamza; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنَ الأرْضِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اتَّخَذَ» in the sense of "made", and the clause «هُمْ يُنْشِرُونَ» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «آلهة».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: (لو كان فيهما آلهة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is resumptive. The preposition and its genitive noun «فِيهما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «كان», and «آلهة» is its noun. His saying «إلا الله» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «آلهة». His saying «فَسُبْحَانَ»: the fāʾ is resumptive, and a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); «رَبِّ» is a badal (substitute). His saying «عمَّا» is composed of the preposition «عن» and the maṣdariyya «ما», and the maṣdar «عن وصفهم» (above their describing) is attached to the implied verb «نسبِّح» (we glorify); the clause «يَصِفُونَ» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «لا يُسْأَلُ» is resumptive, and the clause «وهم يُسْألُونَ» is conjoined to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «أَمْ» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) am; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ دُونهِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object, and «آلهة» is the first object. «هَاتُوا» is an imperative verb with its fāʿil (agent). The clause «هذا ذِكْرُ» is resumptive within the scope of the speech; «مَنْ» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «مَعِيَ» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); «قَبْلِي» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to the ṣila. The clause «بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ» is resumptive, and the clause «فَهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «لا يَعْلَمُونَ».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: His saying «رَسُولٍ»: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «نُوحِي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «أَرْسَلْنَا», and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the interpreted maṣdar is the object of «نوحي». «إِلا أَنَا»: a particle of restriction, and a badal (substitute) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar (predicate); the clause of divine transcendence (jumlat al-tanzīh) is the khabar of «أَنَّ». The clause «فَاعْبُدُونِ» is conjoined to the khabar clause; the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ in «فاعْبُدُونِ» is the object of the verb, and the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya).

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The second object of «اتَّخَذَ» is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: from among the angels. «عِبادٌ» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هم (they). The clause (نُسَبِّحُ سُبْحَانَهُ) is resumptive, and so is the clause «بل هم عباد».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «لا يَسْبِقُونَهُ» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «عِبادٌ»; the preposition and its genitive noun «بالقول» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause «وهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «هُمْ عِبَادٌ».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «يَعْلَمُ» is a third naʿt (adjective); the adverb «بَيْنَ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); the clause «ولا يَشْفَعُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «يعلم»; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ» is attached to the khabar (predicate), and the clause «وهم مُّشْفِقُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «ولا يَشْفَعُونَ».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «وَمَن يَقُلْ» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْهُمْ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يَقُلْ»; the clause «يَقُلْ» is the khabar (predicate) of the conditional mubtadaʾ (subject) «مَنْ»; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ دُونِهِ» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «إِلَهٌ»; and the clause «فَذَلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The kāf in «كذلك» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the implied form being: نجزي الظالمين جزاءً مثل ذلك الجزاء (We recompense the wrongdoers a recompense like that recompense); the clause «نجزي» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «أَوَلَمْ يَرَ» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of yarā. The clause «وَجَعَلْنَا» is conjoined to the clause «فَتَقْنَا», and the clause «أَفَلا يُؤْمِنُونَ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: «رَوَاسِيَ» is the first object of «جَعَلْنَا», and the preposition and its genitive noun «في الأرْضِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object. The interpreted maṣdar «أَنْ تَمِيدَ» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e.: for fear that it should shake. The preposition and its genitive noun «فيها» is attached to the second object; «سُبُلا» is a badal (substitute) of «فِجَاجًا»; the clause «لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «وَهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ» is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun «عن آيَاتِهَا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «وهو الذي» is resumptive; the clause «كُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the preceding nouns; the preposition and its genitive noun «في فلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and the tanwīn of «كُلٌّ» is a compensation for a single word.

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The clause «وما جَعَلْنَا» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «لِبَشَرٍ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) second object; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ قَبْلِكَ» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «بَشَرٍ». The condition and the interrogative come together in His saying «أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ», and the condition was answered in His saying «فهم الخَالِدُونَ»; the clause «أفإن مِتَّ» is conjoined to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «ذَائِقَةُ» is the khabar (predicate) of «كُلُّ»; the clause «وَنَبْلُوكُمْ» is conjoined to the resumptive one; His saying «فِتْنَةً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); and the clause «تُرْجَعُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «نبلوكم».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. His saying «إن يَّتَخِذُونَكَ»: «إن» is negating, and an imperfect verb in the nominative, its fāʿil (agent), its first object, and its second object: «هُزُوًا». Here «إذا» differs from the conditional particles, since when these particles are answered with «ما» or the negating «إنْ», the fāʾ must be brought, as in: إنْ درست فما أخطأت (if you studied, then you did not err), whereas you say: إذا درست ما أخطأت (when you studied, you did not err). The clause «أهذا الذي» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) of an implied (muqaddar) verb of saying, i.e.: يقولون (they say). This implied element is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of «يَتَّخِذُونَكَ», i.e.: قائلين (saying). The clause «وهم بذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ هم كَافِرُونَ» is a ḥāl of the agent of «يَتَّخِذُونَكَ»; the second «هم» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, and «كافرون» is the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ عَجَلٍ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الإنْسَان»; the clause «سَأُرِيكُمْ» is resumptive, and the clause «فَلا تَسْتَعْجِلُون» is conjoined to the clause «سَأُرِيكُم». «لا» is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is the object of the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «متى» is an interrogative noun, an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) khabar (predicate); «هذا» is mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الوَعْدُ» is a badal (substitute). The conditional clause is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: (لو يعلم الذين كفروا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: they would not have sought to hasten the punishment. «حين» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «علموا» and not an adverb, i.e.: if they knew the time when the Fire is not held back. The clause «لا يَكُفُّونَ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause «ولا هُم يُنْصَرُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «لا يَكُفُّونَ».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The clause «بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ» is resumptive; «بَغْتَةً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun of the Hour. The clause «فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «تَبْهَتُهُمْ», and the clause «ولا هم يُنْظَرُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The clause «وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ» is resumptive, and the clause «اسْتُهْزِئَ» is the answer to the oath. The preposition and its genitive noun «بِرُسُلٍ» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ قَبْلِكَ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رسل»; the clause «فَحَاقَ» is conjoined to the clause «اسْتُهْزِئَ»; and His saying «ما كانوا»: a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of «حَاقَ».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «مَنْ» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «يَكْلَؤُكُمْ» is its khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. His saying «بَلْ هُم مُّعْرِضُونَ»: a particle of digression (iḍrāb), a mubtadaʾ and a khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun «عن ذكر» is attached to the khabar. The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «أَمْ» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) am, meaning bal plus the hamza. The clause «تَمْنَعُهُمْ» is a naʿt (adjective); the clause «لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «تمنعهم», and the clause «وَلا هُمْ يُصْحَبُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «لا يستطيعون».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The maṣdar «حتى أن طال» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مَتَّعْنَا». The clause «أَفَلا يَرَوْنَ» is resumptive, and the maṣdar «أنَّا نَأْتي» is the object of «يَرَوْنَ»; the clause «نَنْقُصُهَا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «نأتي»; and the clause «أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «ولا يسمع» is resumptive, and the clause «يُنْذَرُونَ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «إذا» is a pure adverb (ẓarf), and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The clause «وَلَئِن مَّسَّتْهُم» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ عذابٍ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نَفْحَةٌ». The lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped; the implied (muqaddar) wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the nūn is for emphasis (tawkīd). The clause «لَيَقُولُنَّ» is the answer to the oath, and the clause «إِنَّا كُنَّا» is the response to the vocative, resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لِيَوْمِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نضع»; the clause «فلا تُظْلَمُ» is conjoined to the clause «نضع», and the clause «وإِنْ كان مِثْقَالَ» is conjoined to the clause «نضع». His saying «وكَفَى بنا حَاسِبِين»: the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), the pronoun «نا» is the fāʿil (agent), and «حاسبين» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «ولقد آتينا» is resumptive; «الفُرْقَانَ» is the second object; the preposition and its genitive noun «لِلمُتَّقِين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ذكرًا».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «للمتقين»; the preposition and its genitive noun «بِالْغَيْبِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent); the clause «وَهُم مُّشْفِقُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «يَخْشَوْنَ», and the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنَ السَّاعَةِ» is attached to the khabar (predicate) «مشفقون».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «أنزلناهُ» is a second naʿt (adjective), and the clause «أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ» is conjoined to the clause «هذا ذِكْرٌ».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «ولقد آتينا» is conjoined to the clause «لقد آتينا» in verse (48); the preposition and its genitive noun «من قَبْلُ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آتَيْنَا», and the clause «كُنَّا» is conjoined to the clause «آتَيْنَا».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: «إذ» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) {آتَيْنَا}. His saying «ما هذه التَّمَاثِيلُ»: «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the demonstrative is its khabar (predicate); «التماثيل» is a badal (substitute), the relative noun is a naʿt (adjective), and the preposition and its genitive noun «لها» is attached to the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: «عَابِدِينَ» is the second object, and the preposition and its genitive noun «لها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عَابِدِين».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: «أنتم» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the nominative pronoun in «كنتم», and «آباؤكم» is conjoined to the tāʾ; conjoining an overt noun to a nominative pronoun is permitted because of the presence of a separator. The clause «لقد كنتم» is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position, and the oath clause with its response is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb).

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «أَمْ أَنْتَ مِنَ الَّلاعِبِين» is conjoined to the clause «جِئْتَنَا».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: «بل» is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رَبُّ». The clause «وَأَنَا على ذَلِكُمْ من الشَّاهِدِين» is conjoined to the clause «رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ». The maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) is implied (muqaddar), its implied form being: لا يَصِحُّ ذلك (that is not right), and the clause «بل ربُّكم ربُّ» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The «wāw» is a conjunction, and the «tāʾ» is a particle of oath and a preposition; the genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) «أُقْسِمُ» (I swear). The clause «وأقسم بالله» is conjoined to the clause {رَبُّكُمْ رَبُّ}. The clause «تُوَلُّوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative, and the maṣdar «أَنْ تُوَلُّوا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «مُدْبِرِينَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: «جُذَاذًا» is the second object; «إلا» is a particle of exception; «كَبيرًا» is the excepted; the preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كبيرًا». The clause «لَعَلَّهُم يَرجِعُون» is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun «إليه» is attached to «يرجعون».

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: «مَنْ» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «إِنَّهُ لَمِن الظَّالمين» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The clause «يَذْكُرُهُمْ» is a naʿt (adjective), the clause «يُقَالُ» is a second naʿt, and «إبراهيم» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: هو.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: The fāʾ in «فَأْتُوا» links to the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: إن كان كذلك فأتوا (if it is so, then bring), and this implied element is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb). The preposition and its genitive noun «على أَعْيُنِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «به», and the clause «لعلهم يشهدون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: «هذا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause «يا إبراهيم» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: I did not do it; the clause «بل فَعَلَه» is resumptive. His saying «هذا»: a naʿt (adjective) interpreted as a derived word, i.e.: the one pointed to. The clause «فَاسْأَلوهم» is conjoined to the clause «فعله كَبِيرهُم»; the clause «إِنْ كانوا يَنطِقُون» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: The clause «فَرَجعُوا» is resumptive; «أنتم» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf, and «الظالمون» is the khabar (predicate) of inna.

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The clause «لقد عَلِمْتَ» is the response to an implied (muqaddar) oath, and the oath clause with its response is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) of an implied verb of saying that is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: قائلين والله لقد عَلِمْتَ (saying: by Allah, you have known). The clause «ما هؤلاء يَنْطِقُونَ» stands in place of the two objects of ʿalima, and the clause «ينطقون» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: The maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: أتخطئون؟ (do you err?). The clause «فَتَعْبُدُونَ» is conjoined to the implied object of the speech; the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ دُونِ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the following «ما», and «ما» is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «شيئًا» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: a benefit, little or much.

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: «أُفٍّ» is a verbal noun with the force of an imperfect verb (ism fiʿl muḍāriʿ), meaning: I am vexed; the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أُفٍّ». The preposition and its genitive noun «مِن دُونِ» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied (muqaddar) object of «تعبدون». The clause «أف لكم» is resumptive within the scope of the speech; the clause «تعقلون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: The clause «إن كنتم فاعلين» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: «كُوني» is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, with its noun and its khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun «على إبراهيم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «سلامًا».

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: «كَيْدًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «الأخسرين» is the second object of «جعلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: «لُوطًا» is a noun conjoined to the hāʾ in «نَجَّيْنَاهُ»; «التي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الأرض»; and the two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; «نَافِلَةً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «يعقوب». His saying «وكُلا»: the wāw is a conjunction; «كلا» is the first object, placed first; «صالحين» is the second object of «جعلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: «أَئِمَّةً» is the second object, and the clause «يَهْدُونَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أئمة»; the clause «وكانوا» is conjoined to the clause «أَوْحَيْنَا».

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: His saying «وَلُوطًا»: the wāw is resumptive, and «ولوطًا» is the object of an omitted verb explained by what follows; the clause of the implied (muqaddar) verb is resumptive, and the clause «آتيناه» is explicative of it. «حُكْمًا» is the second object; «التي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «القرية»; the clause «إنهم كانوا» is resumptive; «فاسقين» is a naʿt of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «في رحمتنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. The clause «إنه من الصالحين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «أدخلناه».

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: His saying «ونوحًا»: conjoined to «لوطًا». «إذ» is an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of «نُوحًا». «وأهله» is a noun conjoined to the hāʾ in «نجَّيناه».

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: The verb «نصرناه» includes the meaning of «عصمناه» (We protected him), so it was made transitive in the way that one is. «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «القوم»; the clause «إنهم كانوا قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ» is resumptive; the clause «فأغرقناهم» is conjoined to the clause «كانوا»; «أجمعين» is tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:78-78.t: «داود»: a noun conjoined to «نوحًا» in verse (76). The first «إذ» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of «داود وسليمان», and the second «إذ» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يحكمان»; the clause «نَفَشَتْ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «وكنا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the alif in «يحكمان». The lām in «لحكمهم» is redundant (zāʾida) for strengthening (taqwiya); «حكمهم» is the object of «شاهدين», and «شاهدين» is the khabar (predicate) of «كنا».

harrat-mujtaba:79-79.t: The clause «فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا» is conjoined to the clause {يَحْكُمَانِ}; «سليمان» is the second object. His saying «وكلا»: the wāw is parenthetical, and the clause «آتينا» is parenthetical between the two conjoined items; «كلا» is an object placed first, and «حكمًا» is the second object of «آتينا». «مع» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. The clause «يُسَبِّحْنَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الجبال», and the clause «وكُنَّا» is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «سخَّرنا».

harrat-mujtaba:80-80.t: «صَنْعة» is the second object; the preposition and its genitive noun «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «لَبُوسٍ»; the genitive maṣdar in «لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ» is attached to «علَّمناه»; and the clause «فهل أنتم شاكرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:81-81.t: His saying «ولِسُليمان الرِّيحَ»: the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being: سخَّرنا (We subjected); «الريح» is the object of the implied verb. «عاصِفة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الريح», and the clause «تجري» is a second ḥāl of «الريح». The implied clause «وسَخَّرْنَا» is conjoined to the clause «علَّمناه». The preposition and its genitive noun «بأمره» is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «تجري», i.e.: being accompanied. The clause «وكنا» is a ḥāl of the pronoun in the implied «سخَّرْنا».

harrat-mujtaba:82-82.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «ومن الشَّيَاطين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the preceding implied (muqaddar) verb «سخَّرنا»; «مَنْ»: a relative noun conjoined to the preceding {الرِّيحَ}, i.e.: and We subjected to him those who dive for him. «دُونَ» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «عملا»; the clause «وكنَّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «يعملون»; and the preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to the khabar (predicate) «حافظين».

harrat-mujtaba:83-83.t: His saying «وأَيُّوبَ»: a noun conjoined to «نوحًا» in verse (76). «إذ» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of «أيوب». The interpreted maṣdar «أَني مَسَّنِيَ» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ, and the clause «وأنت أرحم الراحمين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the yāʾ in «مسَّني».

harrat-mujtaba:84-84.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «به» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ ضُرٍّ» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما». «معهم» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to a ḥāl of «مثلهم», and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) to it. «رحمةً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The preposition and its genitive noun «من عندنا» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «رحمة»; «وذِكرى» is a noun conjoined to «رحمة»; and the preposition and its genitive noun «للعابدين» is attached to a naʿt of «ذِكرى».

harrat-mujtaba:85-85.t: His saying «وإسماعيل»: conjoined to «أيُّوبَ» in verse (83). «كُلٌّ» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the tanwīn is a compensation for a single word, i.e.: وكلهم (and all of them). The clause «كُلٌّ من الصابرين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the aforementioned prophets.

harrat-mujtaba:86-86.t: The clause «إنهم من الصالحين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «أدخلناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:87-87.t: «ذا النُّون» is a noun conjoined to «إسماعيل»; «إذ» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of «ذا النُّونِ». «أَنْ» is an abrogating particle (nāsikha), lightened (mukhaffafa), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the maṣdar stands in place of the two objects, and the clause «لن نَقْدِرَ» is the khabar (predicate) of «أنْ». The clause of divine transcendence (jumlat al-tanzīh) is explicative of the calling, and the clause «سبحانك» is resumptive. «أنت» is a badal of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar, and the clause «إني كنت» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:88-88.t: His saying «وكذلك»: the wāw is resumptive, the kāf is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e.: ننجِّي المؤمنين إنجاءً مثل ذلك الإنجاء (We save the believers a saving like that saving). The clause «ننجي» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:89-89.t: «وزكريا»: a noun conjoined to «ذا النُّونِ»; «إذ» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of «زكريا». The clause «ربِّ لا تذرني» is explicative of the calling; «فردًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the yāʾ. The clause «لا تَذَرْني» is the response to the vocative, and the clause «وأنت خير» is a ḥāl of the yāʾ in «لا تَذَرْنِي».

harrat-mujtaba:90-90.t: The clause «إنهم كانوا» is resumptive; «رَغَبًا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «وكانوا» is conjoined to the clause «كانوا يُسَارِعُونَ».

harrat-mujtaba:91-91.t: «والتي» is a relative noun conjoined to «زكريا» in verse (89); «وابْنَها» is a noun conjoined to the pronoun hāʾ in «جعلناها»; the preposition and its genitive noun «للعالمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «آية».

harrat-mujtaba:92-92.t: «أُمَّتُكُمْ» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «أُمَّةً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أمتكم». The clause «وأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ» is conjoined to the resumptive one, «إن هذه أمتكم», and the clause «فَاعْبُدُونِ» is conjoined to the clause «أنا ربكم». The implied (muqaddar) yāʾ in «اعبدون» is the object of the verb, and the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya).

harrat-mujtaba:93-93.t: «بَيْنَهُمْ»: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the verb includes the meaning of «قطعوا» (they cut). «كل» is mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun «إلينا» is attached to the khabar (predicate) «راجعون»; and the clause «كل إلينا راجعون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:94-94.t: The clause «فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ» is conjoined to the resumptive one, {كُلٌّ إِلَيْنَا رَاجِعُونَ}. «مَنْ» is conditional, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun «من الصالحات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause «وهو مؤمن» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يعمل»; the clause «فلا كُفْرَانَ لِسَعْيِهِ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the clause «وإنا له كاتبون» is conjoined to the apodosis.

harrat-mujtaba:95-95.t: «وَحَرَامٌ»: the wāw is resumptive, and a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun «على قرية» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «حرام», and beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it is qualified. The clause «أهلكناها» is a naʿt of «قرية». «حرام» means "obligatory", as in: {قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلا تُشْرِكُوا}, and abandoning polytheism is obligatory. The maṣdar «أنهم لا يرجعون» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. Ibn ʿAbbās said in explaining the verse: «واجب على قرية أهلكناها أنه لا يرجع منهم راجع» (it is obligatory upon a town We destroyed that none of them returns).

harrat-mujtaba:96-96.t: «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya); «إذا» is a conditional adverb (ẓarfiyya sharṭiyya) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis, and the conditional clause is resumptive. The clause «فُتِحَتْ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «وهم من كل حَدَبٍ يَنْسِلُون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition and its genitive noun «من كل حدب» is attached to the verb «ينسلون».

harrat-mujtaba:97-97.t: The clause «واقْتَرَبَ الوَعْدُ» is conjoined to the clause {فُتِحَتْ}. The clause «فإذا هي شَاخِصَةٌ أَبصارُ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the preceding condition introduced by the conditional «إذا», and the clause «شاخصة أبصار» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «هي». The fāʾ in «فإذا» links the apodosis, and the «إذا» of surprise (fujāʾiyya) reinforces the linking of the apodosis. «هي» is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), mubtadaʾ; «شاخصة» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «أبصار»; «الذين» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «يا ويلنا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) of an implied (muqaddar) verb of saying, i.e.: يقولون (they say), and the implied clause of saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «كفروا». The clause «قد كنَّا» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the clause «بل كنا ظالمين» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:98-98.t: «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to the kāf; the preposition and its genitive noun «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied (muqaddar) referent pronoun, i.e.: ما تعبدونه كائنًا من دون (what you worship, being other than…). The clause «أنتم واردون» is a ḥāl of «جهنم»; a ḥāl may come from the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) here because the muḍāf is like a part of the muḍāf ilayhi.

harrat-mujtaba:99-99.t: (لو كان هؤلاء آلهة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is resumptive; the clause «ما وَرَدُوهَا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the clause «وكل فيها خالدون» is conjoined to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:100-100.t: The clause «لهم فيها زَفِير» is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun «فيها» is attached to the "being established" (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached; «زفير» is mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «وهم فيها لا يسمعون» is conjoined to the resumptive one, and the preposition and its genitive noun «فيها» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the mubtadaʾ «هم».

harrat-mujtaba:101-101.t: The two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «سبقت», and the clause «أولئك عنها مُبْعَدُونَ» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:102-102.t: The clause «لا يسمعون» is a second khabar (predicate) of {إِنَّ}; the clause «وهم في ما اشْتَهَتْ أَنفسُهم خالدون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يسمعون»; and the clause «اشتهت» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

harrat-mujtaba:103-103.t: The clause «لا يَحْزُنُهُم الفَزَعُ» is a third khabar (predicate) of {إِنَّ}. The clause «هذا يَوْمُكُم» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech verb) of an implied (muqaddar) verb of saying, i.e.: يقولون (they say), and the implied clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الملائكة».

harrat-mujtaba:104-104.t: His saying «يوم»: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being: اذكر (remember), and the clause «اذكر» is resumptive. The kāf in «كَطَيِّ» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «طي» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun «للكتب» is redundant (zāʾida) for strengthening (taqwiya). The kāf in «كما» is a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq, and «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e.: We will repeat it a repeating like Our beginning first. The clause «نعيده» is resumptive. «وَعْدًا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e.: نَعِدُ وعدًا (We promise a promise), and the clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «علينا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective (ṣifa) of «وعدًا»; and the clause «إنا كنَّا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:105-105.t: The two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «كتبنا», and the interpreted maṣdar «أن الأرض يرثها» is the object of «كتب».

harrat-mujtaba:106-106.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لِقَوْمٍ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «بلاغًا».
